description: Constitutional Bodies question bank derived from FDA/SDA Examination Notes (Section 7.5). Covers Election Commission, UPSC, State PSCs, Finance Commission, CAG, Attorney General, Advocate General, State Election Commission, State Finance Commission, GST Council, NCSC/NCST/NCBC, Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, Inter-State Council, District/Metropolitan Planning Committees, and high-yield exam traps. Verify and expand before formal examination use.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is a constitutional body?

options.A: A body created by an Act of Parliament
options.B: An institution whose existence, basic composition, powers or functions are provided for by the Constitution of India
options.C: A body created by a resolution of the Union Cabinet
options.D: A body created by a State Legislature

questions.explanation: A constitutional body is an institution whose existence, basic composition, powers or functions are provided for by the Constitution of India. It derives authority directly from constitutional provisions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: How is a constitutional body different from a statutory body?

options.A: A constitutional body is created by an Act of Parliament, whereas a statutory body is created by the Constitution
options.B: A constitutional body is created or expressly recognised by the Constitution, whereas a statutory body is created by an Act of Parliament or a State Legislature
options.C: Both are created by the President
options.D: A statutory body derives authority directly from the Constitution

questions.explanation: A constitutional body is created or expressly recognised by the Constitution, whereas a statutory body is created by an Act of Parliament or a State Legislature. The Election Commission of India is constitutional under Article 324; the National Human Rights Commission is statutory under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The National Human Rights Commission is an example of which type of body?

options.A: Constitutional body
options.B: Statutory body

questions.explanation: The National Human Rights Commission is statutory under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following pairs of constitutional provisions is correctly matched?

options.A: Election Commission — Articles 315–323
options.B: UPSC — Articles 324–329

questions.explanation: The Finance Commission is provided for under Articles 280–281. Election Commission: Articles 324–329; UPSC and State PSCs: Articles 315–323; CAG: Articles 148–151; Attorney General: Article 76.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Articles provide for the Attorney General of India?

options.A: Article 76
options.B: Article 165

questions.explanation: The Attorney General of India is provided for under Article 76. Article 165 provides for the Advocate General of a State.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for the Advocate General of a State?

options.A: Article 76
options.B: Article 165

questions.explanation: Article 165 provides for the Advocate General of a State.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The State Election Commission is provided for under which Articles?

options.A: Articles 243K and 243ZA
options.B: Articles 243I and 243Y

questions.explanation: The State Election Commission is provided for under Articles 243K (Panchayats) and 243ZA (Municipalities).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The State Finance Commission is provided for under which Article?

options.A: Article 243K
options.B: Article 243I

questions.explanation: Article 243I provides for the State Finance Commission. Article 243Y extends the relevant review role to Municipalities.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The GST Council is provided for under which Article?

options.A: Article 279A
options.B: Article 280

questions.explanation: Article 279A provides for the Goods and Services Tax Council.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes is provided for under which Article?

options.A: Article 338A
options.B: Article 338B

questions.explanation: Article 338 provides for the National Commission for Scheduled Castes. Article 338A: NCST; Article 338B: NCBC.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission of India?

options.A: Article 324
options.B: Article 325

questions.explanation: Article 324, in Part XV of the Constitution, vests the superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of specified elections in the Election Commission.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: When was the Election Commission of India established?

options.A: 26 January 1950
options.B: 25 January 1950

questions.explanation: The Election Commission of India was established on 25 January 1950. National Voters' Day is observed on 25 January every year.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: National Voters' Day is observed on which date?

options.A: 26 January
options.B: 15 August

questions.explanation: National Voters' Day is observed on 25 January every year, marking the establishment of the Election Commission of India on 25 January 1950.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which elections are conducted under the superintendence, direction and control of the Election Commission of India?

options.A: Elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President
options.B: Elections to Panchayats and Municipalities only
options.C: Elections to Parliament and Panchayats only
options.D: Elections to State Legislatures and Municipalities only

questions.explanation: The ECI conducts elections to Parliament, the Legislature of every State, and the offices of President and Vice-President of India. Elections to Panchayats and Municipalities are conducted by the respective State Election Commissions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Elections to Panchayats and Municipalities are conducted by which authority?

options.A: Election Commission of India
options.B: State Election Commissions

questions.explanation: Elections to Panchayats and Municipalities are conducted by the respective State Election Commissions under Articles 243K and 243ZA, not by the Election Commission of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the constitutional composition of the Election Commission of India?

options.A: A Chief Election Commissioner and exactly two Election Commissioners as fixed by the Constitution
options.B: A Chief Election Commissioner and such number of other Election Commissioners as the President may from time to time fix
options.C: Three Election Commissioners with no Chief Election Commissioner
options.D: A Chief Election Commissioner and four Election Commissioners

questions.explanation: Under Article 324(2), the Election Commission consists of the Chief Election Commissioner and such number of other Election Commissioners as the President may from time to time fix. The Constitution itself does not permanently prescribe a fixed number.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: When did the Election Commission become a multi-member body?

options.A: 15 August 1947
options.B: 25 January 1950

questions.explanation: Two additional Election Commissioners were appointed on 1 October 1993; the multi-member arrangement has continued since then. The Commission currently functions with one CEC and two Election Commissioners.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners?

options.A: The Prime Minister
options.B: The President
options.D: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: The President appoints the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners, subject to the applicable parliamentary law. The Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 provides the statutory appointment procedure.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Act provides the statutory appointment procedure for the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners?

options.A: Representation of the People Act, 1951
options.B: Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023

questions.explanation: The Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 provides the statutory appointment procedure.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which committee recommends appointments to the Election Commission under the 2023 Act?

options.A: A committee consisting of the Prime Minister as Chairperson, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha (or leader of the largest opposition party where no recognised LoP exists), and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister
options.B: A committee consisting of the Chief Justice of India, the Prime Minister and the Speaker
options.C: A committee consisting of the President, the Vice-President and the Prime Minister
options.D: A committee consisting of the Cabinet Secretary and the Attorney General

questions.explanation: The committee consists of the Prime Minister as Chairperson, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha (or leader of the largest opposition party where no recognised LoP exists), and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister. A Search Committee headed by the Cabinet Secretary prepares a panel for consideration.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which body prepares the panel of candidates for appointment to the Election Commission under the 2023 Act?

options.A: A Search Committee headed by the Cabinet Secretary
options.B: The Union Public Service Commission
options.D: The Department of Personnel and Training

questions.explanation: A Search Committee headed by the Cabinet Secretary prepares a panel for consideration by the appointment committee.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the term of office of the CEC and Election Commissioners under the 2023 Act?

options.A: Five years or until attaining 60 years of age, whichever is earlier
options.B: Six years from the date of assuming office or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
options.C: Six years or until attaining 62 years of age, whichever is earlier
options.D: Tenure during the pleasure of the President

questions.explanation: Under the 2023 Act, the term is six years from the date of assuming office or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier. They are not eligible for reappointment.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Are the CEC and Election Commissioners eligible for reappointment under the 2023 Act?

options.A: Yes, for one additional term
options.B: Yes, if recommended by the Prime Minister
options.C: No, they are not eligible for reappointment

questions.explanation: Under the 2023 Act, they are not eligible for reappointment.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: How can the Chief Election Commissioner be removed?

options.A: By the President at pleasure
options.B: Only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court, following a parliamentary address supported by the prescribed special majority and an order of the President
options.C: By a simple majority of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: The CEC can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court: on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity, following a parliamentary address supported by the prescribed special majority in each House and an order of the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under the proviso to Article 324(5), an Election Commissioner other than the CEC can be removed only on whose recommendation?

options.A: The President
options.B: The Prime Minister

questions.explanation: Under the proviso to Article 324(5), an Election Commissioner or Regional Commissioner cannot be removed from office except on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner. This protection is distinct from the removal procedure applicable to the CEC.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a principal function of the Election Commission of India?

options.A: Conducting elections to Panchayats and Municipalities
options.B: Preparing and supervising electoral rolls, announcing and administering elections, and recognising political parties and allotting election symbols
options.D: Recommending distribution of taxes between the Union and States

questions.explanation: The ECI prepares and supervises electoral rolls; announces and administers elections; issues the election schedule; recognises political parties and allots election symbols; monitors election expenditure; enforces the Model Code of Conduct; and advises on disqualification matters where assigned.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Does the Election Commission of India conduct elections to local self-government institutions?

options.A: Yes, it conducts all local body elections
options.B: No, elections to Panchayats and Municipalities are vested in State Election Commissions

questions.explanation: No. Under Articles 243K and 243ZA, elections to Panchayats and Municipalities are vested in State Election Commissions. The ECI conducts elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the role of Article 325?

options.A: It provides for adult suffrage
options.B: It provides for one general electoral roll for every territorial constituency and prohibits exclusion from or claim to inclusion in a special electoral roll on grounds only of religion, race, caste or sex
options.C: It empowers Parliament to make laws on elections
options.D: It bars court interference in electoral matters

questions.explanation: Article 325 provides for one general electoral roll for every territorial constituency and prohibits exclusion from, or a claim to inclusion in, a special electoral roll on grounds only of religion, race, caste or sex.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What does Article 326 provide?

options.A: One general electoral roll for every territorial constituency
options.B: Elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies on the basis of adult suffrage
options.C: Power of Parliament to make laws on elections
options.D: Bar on court interference in electoral matters

questions.explanation: Article 326 provides for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies on the basis of adult suffrage, subject to constitutional and statutory qualifications.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 years by which Constitutional Amendment Act?

options.A: 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976
options.B: 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978

questions.explanation: The voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What does Article 327 deal with?

options.A: It empowers Parliament to make laws on elections to legislatures
options.B: It gives State Legislatures power to make laws on State Legislature elections
options.C: It bars court interference in electoral matters

questions.explanation: Article 327 empowers Parliament to make laws on elections to legislatures. Article 328 gives State Legislatures power to make laws on State Legislature elections; Article 329 bars court interference in electoral matters except through election petitions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What does Article 328 deal with?

options.A: Power of Parliament to make laws on elections
options.B: Power of State Legislatures to make laws on State Legislature elections, subject to parliamentary law
options.C: Bar on court interference in electoral matters

questions.explanation: Article 328 gives State Legislatures power to make laws on State Legislature elections, subject to parliamentary law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What does Article 329 generally provide?

options.A: It provides for adult suffrage
options.B: It empowers Parliament to make laws on elections
options.C: It generally bars court interference in electoral matters except through election petitions in the manner provided by law
options.D: It provides for one general electoral roll

questions.explanation: Article 329 generally bars court interference in electoral matters except through election petitions in the manner provided by law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Act deals principally with the allocation of seats and electoral rolls?

options.A: Representation of the People Act, 1951
options.B: Representation of the People Act, 1950

questions.explanation: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 deals principally with allocation of seats and electoral rolls. The Representation of the People Act, 1951 deals with conduct of elections, qualifications and disqualifications, corrupt practices and election disputes.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Act deals with the conduct of elections, qualifications and disqualifications, corrupt practices and election disputes?

options.A: Representation of the People Act, 1950
options.B: Representation of the People Act, 1951
options.D: Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023

questions.explanation: The Representation of the People Act, 1951 deals with conduct of elections, qualifications and disqualifications, corrupt practices and election disputes.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Act governs the elections of the President and Vice-President of India?

options.A: Representation of the People Act, 1950
options.B: Representation of the People Act, 1951

questions.explanation: The Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952 governs those elections.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for a Public Service Commission for the Union and a Public Service Commission for each State?

options.A: Article 315
options.B: Article 316

questions.explanation: Article 315 provides for a Public Service Commission for the Union and a Public Service Commission for each State. Two or more States may agree to have a Joint State Public Service Commission.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who appoints the Chairman and members of the UPSC?

options.A: The Prime Minister
options.B: The President of India
options.D: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: The President of India appoints the Chairman and other members of the UPSC under Article 316.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who determines the number of UPSC members?

options.A: The Constitution fixes a permanent number
options.B: Parliament by law
options.C: The President under Article 318, subject to constitutional safeguards

questions.explanation: The Constitution does not fix a permanent number. Under Article 318, the President may determine the number of members and their conditions of service, subject to constitutional safeguards.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the tenure of a UPSC member?

options.A: Six years from the date of entering office or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
options.B: Six years or until attaining 62 years of age, whichever is earlier
options.C: Five years or until attaining 60 years of age, whichever is earlier
options.D: During the pleasure of the President

questions.explanation: Under Article 316, UPSC members hold office for six years from the date they enter office or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier. They may resign by writing to the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: How may a UPSC member resign from office?

options.A: By writing to the Prime Minister
options.B: By writing to the President
options.C: By writing to the Chief Justice of India
options.D: By writing to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: Under Article 316, a UPSC member may resign by writing to the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What proportion of UPSC members should have government service experience?

options.A: At least one-third
options.B: As nearly as may be, one-half

questions.explanation: As nearly as may be, one-half of the members should be persons who have held office for at least ten years under the Government of India or a State Government. This is a constitutional qualification guideline under Article 316.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: For how long must a person have held office under the Government of India or a State Government to count toward the one-half UPSC membership guideline?

options.A: At least five years
options.B: At least ten years

questions.explanation: As nearly as may be, one-half of the members should be persons who have held office for at least ten years under the Government of India or a State Government (Article 316).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: How can the UPSC Chairman or a member be removed on the ground of misbehaviour?

options.A: By the President at pleasure
options.B: By the President after the Supreme Court, on a reference by the President, conducts an inquiry and reports that the member ought to be removed
options.C: By a simple majority of Parliament

questions.explanation: Under Article 317, the President may remove a member on grounds of misbehaviour after the Supreme Court, on a reference by the President, conducts an inquiry and reports that the member ought to be removed.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Besides misbehaviour, in which of the following specified cases may the President remove a UPSC member under Article 317?

options.A: Insolvency, paid employment outside official duties, or infirmity of mind or body
options.B: Only on a Supreme Court recommendation
options.D: Only on the Prime Minister's advice

questions.explanation: The President may also remove a member in specified cases such as insolvency, paid employment outside official duties, or infirmity of mind or body.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who can suspend a UPSC member while an inquiry is pending?

options.A: The Prime Minister
options.B: The President

questions.explanation: The President may suspend the Chairman or another member of the UPSC while a reference concerning removal is pending before the Supreme Court.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article lists the main functions of the UPSC?

options.A: Article 315
options.B: Article 316

questions.explanation: The main functions of the UPSC are set out under Article 320.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the UPSC under Article 320?

options.A: Conducting examinations for appointments to Union services
options.B: Advising on disciplinary matters affecting civil servants

questions.explanation: Auditing government expenditure is the function of the CAG, not the UPSC. UPSC functions include conducting examinations, assisting in recruitment methods, advising on appointments, promotions and transfers, advising on disciplinary matters, and other assigned functions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Is UPSC advice binding on the Government?

options.A: Yes, it is binding in all matters
options.B: No, it is generally advisory; the Government must place the annual report and a memorandum explaining non-acceptance of advice before Parliament
options.C: Yes, but only on disciplinary matters
options.D: No, and the Government need not report non-acceptance

questions.explanation: No. UPSC is generally an advisory body. Its recommendations are not binding, but the Government is constitutionally required under Article 323 to place its annual report and a memorandum explaining non-acceptance of its advice before Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What does Article 319 provide?

options.A: It restricts further employment after a person ceases to hold office as a member or Chairman of a Public Service Commission
options.B: It provides for the expenses of the UPSC
options.C: It provides for the annual report of the UPSC
options.D: It provides for the removal of UPSC members

questions.explanation: Article 319 restricts further employment after a person ceases to hold office as a member or Chairman of a Public Service Commission. The restrictions differ for the UPSC Chairman, UPSC members and State PSC members.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: How are the expenses of the UPSC treated?

options.A: They are voted annually by Parliament
options.B: They are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India under Article 322
options.C: They are charged on the Contingency Fund of India
options.D: They are met from the Public Account of India

questions.explanation: Under Article 322, the expenses of the UPSC, including salaries, allowances and pensions of its members and staff, are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the key difference between the UPSC and a departmental recruitment agency?

options.A: The UPSC is a constitutional commission with functions under Articles 315–323, whereas a departmental recruitment board is generally created by executive or statutory arrangements
options.B: The UPSC is a statutory body, whereas a departmental board is constitutional
options.D: The UPSC is an executive body

questions.explanation: UPSC is a constitutional commission with functions under Articles 315–323. A departmental recruitment board or other agency is generally created by executive or statutory arrangements and does not have the same constitutional status.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who appoints the Chairman and members of a State Public Service Commission?

options.A: The President of India
options.B: The Governor of the State
options.D: The Chief Justice of the High Court

questions.explanation: The Governor of the State appoints the Chairman and members of the State Public Service Commission under Article 316.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the tenure of a State Public Service Commission member?

options.A: Six years from the date of entering office or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
options.B: Six years from the date of entering office or until attaining 62 years of age, whichever is earlier
options.C: Five years or until attaining 60 years of age, whichever is earlier
options.D: During the pleasure of the Governor

questions.explanation: A State Public Service Commission member holds office for six years from the date of entering office or until attaining 62 years of age, whichever is earlier.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who has the power to remove the Chairman or a member of a State Public Service Commission?

options.A: The Governor of the State
options.B: The President of India
options.D: The Chief Justice of the High Court

questions.explanation: The President of India — not the Governor — has the power of removal under Article 317. For removal on the ground of misbehaviour, the Supreme Court inquiry procedure applies.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a common exam trap regarding State PSC members?

options.A: The Governor appoints them, but the President removes them
options.B: The President appoints them, but the Governor removes them
options.C: The Governor both appoints and removes them
options.D: Parliament both appoints and removes them

questions.explanation: The Governor appoints a State PSC member under Article 316, but the President has the power of removal under Article 317. This is a high-yield exam trap.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What are the principal functions of a State Public Service Commission?

options.A: Auditing State government accounts
options.B: Conducting examinations for appointments to State services and advising on recruitment methods, appointments, promotions, transfers and disciplinary matters
options.D: Recommending distribution of taxes between the Union and States

questions.explanation: A State PSC conducts examinations for appointments to State services and advises the State Government on recruitment methods, appointments, promotions, transfers and disciplinary matters, subject to constitutional provisions and applicable rules.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: To whom does a State Public Service Commission submit its annual report?

options.A: The President of India
options.B: The Governor of the State

questions.explanation: A State PSC submits its annual report to the Governor under Article 323. The Governor causes the report and a memorandum explaining cases where the advice was not accepted to be laid before the State Legislature.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under which Article may two or more States agree to have one Public Service Commission serving their needs?

options.A: Article 315(1)
options.B: Article 315(2)

questions.explanation: Under Article 315(2), two or more States may agree to have one Public Service Commission serving their needs. Parliament may provide for its establishment by law. Its members are appointed by the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who appoints the members of a Joint State Public Service Commission?

options.A: The Governors of the concerned States jointly
options.B: The President of India

questions.explanation: Under Article 315(2), Parliament may provide for the establishment of a Joint State Public Service Commission by law. Its members are appointed by the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which statement correctly contrasts UPSC and State PSC on appointment, retirement age and reporting?

options.A: UPSC members are appointed by the President, retire at 65, and report to the President for placement before Parliament; State PSC members are appointed by the Governor, retire at 62, and report to the Governor for placement before the State Legislature
options.B: UPSC members are appointed by the Governor and retire at 62; State PSC members are appointed by the President and retire at 65
options.C: Both are appointed by the President and retire at 65
options.D: Both are appointed by the Governor and retire at 62

questions.explanation: UPSC members are appointed by the President, retire at 65, and report to the President for placement before Parliament. State PSC members are appointed by the Governor, retire at 62, and report to the Governor for placement before the State Legislature. In both cases, removal is by the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: In both UPSC and State PSC, removal of members is by which authority?

options.A: The President of India
options.B: The Governor

questions.explanation: In both cases, removal is by the President. For State PSC members, the Governor appoints but the President removes.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for the Finance Commission of India?

options.A: Article 279A
options.B: Article 280

questions.explanation: Article 280, in Part XII of the Constitution, provides for the Finance Commission.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who constitutes the Finance Commission and how often?

options.A: Parliament, every five years
options.B: The President, every fifth year or at such earlier time as the President considers necessary
options.D: The Union Finance Minister, every third year

questions.explanation: The President constitutes the Finance Commission by order every fifth year or at such earlier time as the President considers necessary. It consists of a Chairman and four other members.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: How many members does the Finance Commission consist of?

options.A: A Chairman and two other members
options.B: A Chairman and three other members
options.C: A Chairman and four other members
options.D: A Chairman and five other members

questions.explanation: The Finance Commission consists of a Chairman and four other members.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a principal function of the Finance Commission?

options.A: Conducting elections to Parliament
options.B: Recommending the distribution between the Union and States of the net proceeds of shareable taxes
options.D: Appointing judges to the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: The Finance Commission recommends the distribution between the Union and States of the net proceeds of shareable taxes, allocation of the States' shares among the States, principles governing grants-in-aid to States, and measures to augment State Consolidated Funds to supplement Panchayat and Municipal resources.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Are Finance Commission recommendations binding?

options.A: Yes, they are binding on the President
options.B: Yes, they are binding on Parliament
options.C: No, they are recommendations to the President; the President causes them and an explanatory memorandum on action taken to be laid before Parliament under Article 281
options.D: No, and they need not be placed before Parliament

questions.explanation: No. They are recommendations to the President. Under Article 281, the President causes the recommendations and an explanatory memorandum on action taken to be laid before each House of Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is vertical devolution?

options.A: The distribution of the States' share of the divisible pool among individual States
options.B: The division of the divisible pool of Union taxes between the Union Government and all State Governments collectively
options.C: The division of taxes between the Union and local bodies
options.D: The distribution of grants-in-aid among States

questions.explanation: Vertical devolution is the division of the divisible pool of Union taxes between the Union Government and all State Governments collectively.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is horizontal devolution?

options.A: The division of the divisible pool between the Union and States collectively
options.B: The distribution of the States' share of the divisible pool among individual States according to criteria recommended by the Finance Commission
options.C: The distribution of taxes between the Union and Panchayats
options.D: The division of GST revenues between the Union and States

questions.explanation: Horizontal devolution is the distribution of the States' share of the divisible pool among individual States according to the criteria recommended by the Finance Commission.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What are grants-in-aid under Article 275?

options.A: Grants from the Consolidated Fund of India to States in need of assistance, as provided by Parliament, with principles recommended by the Finance Commission
options.B: Grants from the Contingency Fund of India
options.C: Grants given by the RBI to State Governments
options.D: Grants given by the GST Council to States

questions.explanation: Grants-in-aid under Article 275 are grants from the Consolidated Fund of India to States in need of assistance, as provided by Parliament. The Finance Commission recommends principles governing such grants.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the divisible pool of Union taxes?

options.A: All Union taxes including cesses and surcharges
options.B: The net proceeds of Union taxes shareable with States under the constitutional scheme, excluding constitutionally excluded taxes and duties and subject to applicable provisions; cesses and surcharges levied for Union purposes are generally outside it

options.B: Articles 243I and 243Y

questions.explanation: The State Election Commission is provided for under Articles 243K and 243ZA.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which constitutional provision corresponds to the GST Council?

options.A: Article 279A
options.B: Article 280

questions.explanation: The GST Council is provided for under Article 279A.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Articles provide for the NCSC, NCST and NCBC respectively?

options.A: Articles 338, 338A and 338B
options.B: Articles 338A, 338B and 338

questions.explanation: NCSC — Article 338; NCST — Article 338A; NCBC — Article 338B.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which constitutional provision corresponds to the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities?

options.A: Article 338
options.B: Article 350B

questions.explanation: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is provided for under Article 350B.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which constitutional provision corresponds to the Inter-State Council?

options.A: Article 263
options.B: Article 279A

questions.explanation: The Inter-State Council is provided for under Article 263.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which constitutional provision corresponds to the District Planning Committees and Metropolitan Planning Committees?

options.A: Articles 243ZD and 243ZE
options.B: Articles 243I and 243Y

questions.explanation: District Planning Committees — Article 243ZD; Metropolitan Planning Committees — Article 243ZE.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which statement about constitutional bodies is correct?

options.A: Their framework cannot ordinarily be abolished or fundamentally altered by an ordinary executive order; constitutional amendment or legislation authorised by the Constitution may be required
options.B: They can be abolished by a simple executive order
options.C: They are created only by an Act of Parliament

questions.explanation: A constitutional body's framework cannot ordinarily be abolished or fundamentally altered by an ordinary executive order; constitutional amendment or legislation authorised by the Constitution may be required.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a constitutional body?

options.A: National Human Rights Commission
options.B: NITI Aayog

questions.explanation: The Election Commission of India is constitutional under Article 324. NHRC is statutory; NITI Aayog is an executive body; CBI is statutory.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Election Commission of India?

options.A: Preparing and supervising electoral rolls
options.B: Recognising political parties and allotting election symbols
options.C: Conducting elections to Panchayats and Municipalities

questions.explanation: Conducting elections to Panchayats and Municipalities is the function of State Election Commissions, not the ECI.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following does the ECI enforce through its directions?

options.A: The Model Code of Conduct
options.B: The Fundamental Duties
options.C: The Directive Principles of State Policy

questions.explanation: The ECI enforces the Model Code of Conduct through its directions, among its other functions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 324(2), the Constitution itself:

options.A: Permanently fixes the number of Election Commissioners at two
options.B: Does not permanently prescribe a fixed number of Election Commissioners; the President fixes the number from time to time

questions.explanation: The Constitution itself does not permanently prescribe a fixed number. Under Article 324(2), the President may from time to time fix the number of Election Commissioners.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the UPSC is correct?

options.A: The UPSC is a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament
options.B: The UPSC is a constitutional commission with functions under Articles 315–323, and its expenses are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India under Article 322
options.C: The UPSC's recommendations are binding on the Government
options.D: The UPSC is headed by the Chief Election Commissioner

questions.explanation: The UPSC is a constitutional commission with functions under Articles 315–323, and its expenses are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India under Article 322. Its advice is advisory, not binding.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 323, what must the Government place before Parliament regarding UPSC advice?

options.A: Only the annual report of the UPSC
options.B: The annual report and a memorandum explaining non-acceptance of its advice
options.C: Only a memorandum explaining non-acceptance of advice

questions.explanation: Under Article 323, the Government is constitutionally required to place the UPSC annual report and a memorandum explaining non-acceptance of its advice before Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about State Public Service Commissions is correct?

options.A: Members are appointed by the President and removed by the Governor
options.B: Members are appointed by the Governor and removed by the President
options.C: Members are appointed and removed by the Governor
options.D: Members are appointed and removed by the President

questions.explanation: State PSC members are appointed by the Governor under Article 316 and removed by the President under Article 317.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 323, to whom does a State PSC submit its annual report, and where is it laid?

options.A: To the President, laid before Parliament
options.B: To the Governor, laid before the State Legislature
options.C: To the Chief Minister, laid before the State Cabinet
options.D: To the Chief Justice, laid before the High Court

questions.explanation: A State PSC submits its annual report to the Governor under Article 323. The Governor causes the report and a memorandum explaining cases where the advice was not accepted to be laid before the State Legislature.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a principal function of the Finance Commission?

options.A: Recommending distribution between the Union and States of the net proceeds of shareable taxes
options.B: Recommending principles governing grants-in-aid to States
options.D: Recommending measures to augment State Consolidated Funds to supplement Panchayat and Municipal resources

questions.explanation: Auditing government receipts and expenditure is the function of the CAG. The Finance Commission recommends tax distribution, principles governing grants-in-aid, and measures to augment State Consolidated Funds.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 281, the President causes what to be laid before each House of Parliament?

options.A: Only the Finance Commission's recommendations
options.B: The Finance Commission's recommendations and an explanatory memorandum on action taken

questions.explanation: Under Article 281, the President causes the recommendations and an explanatory memorandum on action taken to be laid before each House of Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is generally outside the divisible pool of Union taxes?

options.A: Income tax
options.B: Corporation tax
options.C: Cesses and surcharges levied for Union purposes

questions.explanation: Cesses and surcharges levied for Union purposes are generally outside the divisible pool. The divisible pool is the net proceeds of Union taxes shareable with States under the constitutional scheme.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The Sixteenth Finance Commission's recommendations cover which period?

options.A: 1 April 2021 to 31 March 2026
options.B: 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031

questions.explanation: The Sixteenth Finance Commission's recommendations cover the five-year period beginning 1 April 2026 and ending 31 March 2031.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The Finance Commission is constituted under which Part of the Constitution?

options.A: Part V
options.B: Part XII

questions.explanation: Article 280, in Part XII of the Constitution, provides for the Finance Commission.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Article 324 is located in which Part of the Constitution?

options.A: Part V
options.B: Part XII

questions.explanation: Article 324 is in Part XV of the Constitution, which deals with elections.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The CAG holds office for six years or until attaining 65 years of age under which Act?

options.A: The Comptroller and Auditor-General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971
options.B: The CAG Act, 1956

questions.explanation: The CAG holds office for six years from the date of assuming office or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier, under the Comptroller and Auditor-General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about the CAG?

options.A: The CAG is appointed by the President by warrant under his or her hand and seal
options.B: The CAG can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court Judge
options.C: The CAG is eligible for further office under the Government after retirement
options.D: The CAG audits receipts as well as expenditure

questions.explanation: Article 148(4) provides that the CAG is not eligible for further office, either under the Government of India or under the Government of any State, after ceasing to hold office.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Attorney General is NOT correct?

options.A: The Attorney General has the right of audience in all courts in the territory of India
options.B: The Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President
options.C: The Attorney General has the right to vote in Parliament under Article 88
options.D: The Attorney General is not a member of the Council of Ministers merely by holding that office

questions.explanation: Under Article 88, the Attorney General has the right to speak and take part in proceedings but does not have the right to vote by virtue of that Article.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following restrictions applies to the Attorney General's private legal practice?

options.A: The Attorney General must not advise or hold a brief against the Government of India or in cases in which the Government is concerned
options.B: The Attorney General cannot practice law at all
options.C: The Attorney General can appear against the Government with the President's permission
options.D: There are no restrictions on the Attorney General's practice

questions.explanation: The Attorney General may undertake private legal practice subject to applicable rules and restrictions, but must not advise or hold a brief against the Government of India or in cases in which the Government is concerned, and must observe other professional restrictions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

options.A: Election Commission — Article 280
options.B: Finance Commission — Article 324

questions.explanation: CAG — Articles 148–151. Election Commission — Articles 324–329; Finance Commission — Articles 280–281; UPSC — Articles 315–323; Attorney General — Article 76.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

options.A: State Election Commission — Articles 243I and 243Y
options.B: State Finance Commission — Articles 243K and 243ZA

questions.explanation: State Finance Commission — Articles 243I and 243Y. State Election Commission — Articles 243K and 243ZA. GST Council — Article 279A.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

options.A: NCSC — Article 338A
options.B: NCST — Article 338
options.D: Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities — Article 338

questions.explanation: NCBC — Article 338B. NCSC — Article 338; NCST — Article 338A; Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities — Article 350B.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

options.A: Inter-State Council — Article 279A
options.B: District Planning Committees — Article 243ZE

questions.explanation: Metropolitan Planning Committees — Article 243ZE. Inter-State Council — Article 263; District Planning Committees — Article 243ZD; GST Council — Article 279A.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which statement about the removal of Election Commissioners is correct?

options.A: The CEC and other Election Commissioners are removed in the same manner
options.B: The CEC can be removed only like a Supreme Court Judge, while an Election Commissioner other than the CEC cannot be removed except on the recommendation of the CEC
options.C: All Election Commissioners are removed by the Prime Minister
options.D: The CEC can be removed by the President at pleasure

questions.explanation: The CEC can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court. Under the proviso to Article 324(5), an Election Commissioner other than the CEC cannot be removed except on the recommendation of the CEC.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which statement about the removal of UPSC members is correct?

options.A: The President may remove a member on grounds of misbehaviour after a Supreme Court inquiry on a reference by the President
options.B: The President may remove a member at pleasure without any inquiry
options.C: Parliament removes a member by simple majority
options.D: The Chief Justice of India removes a member

questions.explanation: Under Article 317, the President may remove a member on grounds of misbehaviour after the Supreme Court, on a reference by the President, conducts an inquiry and reports that the member ought to be removed.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which statement about the suspension of a UPSC member is correct?

options.A: The President may suspend the Chairman or another member while a reference concerning removal is pending before the Supreme Court
options.B: The Prime Minister may suspend a member
options.C: The Supreme Court may suspend a member
options.D: A member cannot be suspended during an inquiry

questions.explanation: The President may suspend the Chairman or another member of the UPSC while a reference concerning removal is pending before the Supreme Court.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which statement about the retirement age of PSC members is correct?

options.A: UPSC members retire at 62; State PSC members retire at 65
options.B: UPSC members retire at 65; State PSC members retire at 62

questions.explanation: UPSC members retire at 65; State PSC members retire at 62.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which statement about the Finance Commission's recommendations is correct?

options.A: They are binding on the President
options.B: They are recommendations to the President, and under Article 281 the recommendations and an explanatory memorandum on action taken are laid before Parliament
options.D: They require ratification by the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: Finance Commission recommendations are not binding. They are recommendations to the President. Under Article 281, the President causes the recommendations and an explanatory memorandum on action taken to be laid before each House of Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which statement about the CAG's audit mandate is correct?

options.A: The CAG audits only expenditure, not receipts
options.B: The CAG audits receipts as well as expenditure, including revenue collection, transactions from public funds, government accounts, stores and stock, and entities covered by the Constitution and the 1971 Act
options.C: The CAG audits only Union accounts, not State accounts
options.D: The CAG audits only defence expenditure

questions.explanation: The CAG audits receipts as well as expenditure, including revenue collection, transactions from public funds, government accounts, stores and stock, and entities covered by the Constitution and the 1971 Act.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which statement about the CAG and the Public Accounts Committee is correct?

options.A: The CAG is a member of the PAC
options.B: The PAC is a constitutional body
options.C: The CAG assists the PAC by providing audit findings and explanations; the PAC is a parliamentary committee, not a constitutional body

questions.explanation: CAG reports are examined by legislative financial committees, especially the PAC. The CAG assists the PAC by providing audit findings and explanations. The PAC is a parliamentary committee, not a constitutional body.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which statement about the Attorney General's participation in Parliament is correct?

options.A: The Attorney General can vote in Parliament under Article 88
options.B: The Attorney General has the right to speak and take part in proceedings of either House, any joint sitting, and any parliamentary committee of which he or she may be named a member, but not the right to vote by virtue of Article 88
options.C: The Attorney General cannot enter Parliament
options.D: The Attorney General is a member of the Lok Sabha by virtue of office

questions.explanation: Under Article 88, the Attorney General has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of either House of Parliament, any joint sitting, and any parliamentary committee of which he or she may be named a member, but does not have the right to vote by virtue of that Article.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which statement about the Advocate General is correct?

options.A: The Advocate General is appointed by the President and holds office during the pleasure of the President
options.B: The Advocate General is appointed by the Governor, must be qualified to be a High Court judge, and holds office during the pleasure of the Governor
options.C: The Advocate General must be qualified to be a Supreme Court judge
options.D: The Advocate General has a fixed tenure of six years

questions.explanation: The Governor appoints the Advocate General, who must be qualified to be appointed a Judge of a High Court. The Advocate General advises the State Government on legal matters and holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which statement about the State Election Commissioner is correct?

options.A: The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the President
options.B: The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor and has constitutionally protected removal conditions comparable to those of a High Court judge
options.C: The State Election Commissioner holds office during the pleasure of the Chief Minister
options.D: The State Election Commissioner has no constitutional protection

questions.explanation: The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor and has constitutionally protected removal conditions comparable to those of a High Court judge.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which statement about the GST Council's recommendations is correct?

options.A: They are equivalent to legislation
options.B: They are constitutionally significant but are not equivalent to legislation
options.C: They are binding on the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: The GST Council's recommendations are constitutionally significant but are not equivalent to legislation.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: To whom does the National Commission for Scheduled Castes report?

options.A: The Prime Minister
options.B: The President

questions.explanation: The NCSC investigates and monitors constitutional and legal safeguards for Scheduled Castes, inquires into complaints, advises on socio-economic development and reports to the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: To whom does the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes submit its reports?

options.A: The President
options.B: The Governor

questions.explanation: The NCST monitors safeguards for Scheduled Tribes, investigates complaints, advises on development and submits reports to the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under what condition may the President establish an Inter-State Council?

options.A: If it appears that public interests would be served by its establishment
options.B: Only on a Supreme Court recommendation
options.C: Only if Parliament passes a resolution

questions.explanation: Article 263 empowers the President to establish an Inter-State Council if it appears that public interests would be served by its establishment.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the function of District Planning Committees under Article 243ZD?

options.A: To consolidate plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities in a district
options.B: To prepare draft development plans for metropolitan areas

questions.explanation: Article 243ZD provides for District Planning Committees to consolidate plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities in a district.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the function of Metropolitan Planning Committees under Article 243ZE?

options.A: To consolidate plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities in a district
options.B: To prepare draft development plans for metropolitan areas

questions.explanation: Article 243ZE provides for Metropolitan Planning Committees to prepare draft development plans for metropolitan areas.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about charges on the Consolidated Fund is correct?

options.A: The expenses of the UPSC and State PSCs are charged on the Consolidated Fund under Article 322, and the CAG's administrative expenses are protected under Article 148(6)
options.B: The expenses of the Election Commission are charged on the Consolidated Fund under Article 322
options.C: The expenses of the Finance Commission are charged on the Consolidated Fund under Article 148(6)
options.D: Only the CAG's expenses are charged on the Consolidated Fund

questions.explanation: The expenses of the UPSC and State Public Service Commissions are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India or the State, as applicable, under Article 322. The CAG's administrative expenses are also constitutionally protected under Article 148(6).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a high-yield exam trap regarding the Election Commission?

options.A: The ECI conducts local body elections
options.B: The ECI conducts elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President, while State Election Commissions conduct Panchayat and Municipal elections
options.C: The ECI conducts only Parliamentary elections
options.D: The ECI conducts only Presidential elections

questions.explanation: The ECI conducts elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President. State Election Commissions conduct elections to Panchayats and Municipalities within the State.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a high-yield exam trap regarding the removal of State PSC members?

options.A: The Governor appoints and removes State PSC members
options.B: The Governor appoints State PSC members, but the President removes them
options.C: The President appoints and removes State PSC members

questions.explanation: The Governor appoints a State PSC member under Article 316, but the President has the power of removal under Article 317. This is a high-yield exam trap.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a high-yield exam trap regarding the Attorney General?

options.A: The Attorney General is a member of the Union Cabinet
options.B: The Attorney General is the chief legal adviser but is not a member of the Council of Ministers merely by holding that office
options.C: The Attorney General has a fixed tenure of five years
options.D: The Attorney General can vote in Parliament

questions.explanation: The Attorney General is the chief legal adviser to the Union Government but is not a member of the Council of Ministers merely by holding that office. The Constitution does not prescribe a fixed tenure; the Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President and has no right to vote in Parliament under Article 88.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a high-yield exam trap regarding the Finance Commission and GST Council?

options.A: Both are constituted under Article 280
options.B: The Finance Commission (Article 280) recommends tax devolution and grants, while the GST Council (Article 279A) recommends GST rates, exemptions and model laws
options.C: The GST Council recommends tax devolution
options.D: The Finance Commission recommends GST rates

questions.explanation: The Finance Commission is constituted under Article 280 and recommends tax devolution and grants. The GST Council is a constitutional joint forum under Article 279A that makes recommendations on key GST matters, including rates, exemptions and model laws.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a high-yield exam trap regarding the CAG?

options.A: The CAG is a member of Parliament
options.B: The CAG is an independent constitutional authority, neither a member of Parliament nor a judicial officer, and is not eligible for further office after retirement
options.C: The CAG is part of the judiciary
options.D: The CAG can be appointed to another government office after retirement

questions.explanation: The CAG is an independent constitutional authority and is neither a member of Parliament nor a judicial officer. Article 148(4) provides that the CAG is not eligible for further office after ceasing to hold office.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a high-yield exam trap regarding the UPSC's advice?

options.A: UPSC advice is binding on the Government
options.B: UPSC advice is generally advisory; the Government must place the annual report and a memorandum explaining non-acceptance of advice before Parliament under Article 323
options.C: UPSC advice is binding only on disciplinary matters
options.D: The Government need not report non-acceptance of UPSC advice

questions.explanation: UPSC is generally an advisory body. Its recommendations are not binding, but the Government is constitutionally required under Article 323 to place its annual report and a memorandum explaining non-acceptance of its advice before Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a high-yield exam trap regarding the Finance Commission's recommendations?

options.A: Finance Commission recommendations are binding
options.B: Finance Commission recommendations are not binding; they are recommendations to the President, laid before Parliament with an explanatory memorandum under Article 281
options.C: Finance Commission recommendations require Supreme Court approval
options.D: Finance Commission recommendations are automatically enacted into law

questions.explanation: Finance Commission recommendations are not binding. They are recommendations to the President. Under Article 281, the President causes the recommendations and an explanatory memorandum on action taken to be laid before each House of Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a high-yield exam trap regarding the State Finance Commission?

options.A: The State Finance Commission is constituted under Article 280 by the President
options.B: The State Finance Commission is constituted under Article 243I by the Governor every fifth year to review the financial position of Panchayats
options.C: The State Finance Commission is constituted by the GST Council
options.D: The State Finance Commission is constituted by Parliament

questions.explanation: Under Article 243I, the Governor constitutes a State Finance Commission every fifth year to review the financial position of Panchayats and recommend principles for sharing State revenues, grants and measures to improve their financial position.

questions.question: Which of the following is a high-yield exam trap regarding the Election Commission's establishment date?

options.C: The Election Commission was established on 15 August 1947
options.D: The Election Commission was established on 26 November 1949

options.B: Auditing government expenditure

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a function of the Election Commission of India?

options.A: Supervising polling and counting
options.B: Auditing government receipts

questions.explanation: The ECI supervises polling and counting among its principal functions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a function of the UPSC under Article 320?

options.A: Assisting in recruitment methods
options.B: Auditing government expenditure

questions.explanation: UPSC functions under Article 320 include conducting examinations for appointments to Union services, assisting in recruitment methods, advising on appointments, promotions and transfers, advising on disciplinary matters affecting civil servants, and performing other functions assigned by the Constitution or law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a function of the UPSC under Article 320?

options.A: Advising on appointments, promotions and transfers
options.B: Auditing government receipts

questions.explanation: UPSC advises on appointments, promotions and transfers among its functions under Article 320.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a function of the UPSC under Article 320?

options.A: Advising on disciplinary matters affecting civil servants
options.B: Auditing government expenditure
options.D: Recommending distribution of taxes between the Union and States

questions.explanation: UPSC advises on disciplinary matters affecting civil servants among its functions under Article 320.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a principal function of a State Public Service Commission?

options.A: Conducting examinations for appointments to State services
options.B: Auditing State government expenditure
options.C: Conducting elections to the State Legislature

questions.explanation: A State PSC conducts examinations for appointments to State services and advises the State Government on recruitment methods, appointments, promotions, transfers and disciplinary matters.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a principal function of a State Public Service Commission?

options.A: Advising the State Government on recruitment methods, appointments, promotions, transfers and disciplinary matters
options.B: Auditing State government receipts
options.D: Recommending distribution of taxes between the Union and States

questions.explanation: A State PSC advises the State Government on recruitment methods, appointments, promotions, transfers and disciplinary matters, subject to constitutional provisions and applicable rules.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a principal function of the Finance Commission?

options.A: Recommending allocation of the States' shares among the States
options.B: Auditing government expenditure

questions.explanation: The Finance Commission recommends the distribution between the Union and States of the net proceeds of shareable taxes, allocation of the States' shares among the States, principles governing grants-in-aid to States, and measures to augment State Consolidated Funds.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a principal function of the Finance Commission?

options.A: Recommending principles governing grants-in-aid to States
options.B: Auditing government receipts

questions.explanation: The Finance Commission recommends principles governing grants-in-aid to States under Article 275.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a principal function of the Finance Commission?

options.A: Recommending measures to augment State Consolidated Funds to supplement Panchayat and Municipal resources
options.B: Auditing government expenditure

questions.explanation: The Finance Commission recommends measures to augment State Consolidated Funds to supplement Panchayat and Municipal resources on the basis of State Finance Commission recommendations.

questions.question: Which of the following is a major type of audit performed by the CAG?

options.A: Financial audit

questions.question: Which of the following is a major type of audit performed by the CAG?

options.A: Compliance audit
options.B: Electoral audit

questions.explanation: The principal categories include financial audit, compliance audit and performance audit.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a major type of audit performed by the CAG?

options.A: Performance audit
options.B: Electoral audit

questions.explanation: The principal categories include financial audit, compliance audit and performance audit. Performance audit examines economy, efficiency and effectiveness in the use of public resources.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a principal duty of the Attorney General of India?

options.A: Advising the Government of India on legal matters referred by the President
options.B: Auditing government expenditure

questions.explanation: The Attorney General advises the Government of India on legal matters referred by the President, performs legal duties assigned by the President, and discharges functions conferred by the Constitution or other laws.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a principal duty of the Attorney General of India?

options.A: Performing legal duties assigned by the President
options.B: Auditing government receipts

questions.explanation: The Attorney General performs legal duties assigned by the President and discharges functions conferred by the Constitution or other laws.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a principal duty of the Attorney General of India?

options.A: Discharging functions conferred by the Constitution or other laws
options.B: Auditing government expenditure

questions.explanation: The Attorney General discharges functions conferred by the Constitution or other laws.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a matter on which the GST Council makes recommendations?

options.A: GST rates
options.B: Audit of government expenditure

questions.explanation: The GST Council makes recommendations on GST rates, exemptions, model GST laws, principles of levy, apportionment of inter-State supplies, special provisions for certain States and other GST-related matters.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a matter on which the GST Council makes recommendations?
