options.B: Audit of government receipts

questions.explanation: The GST Council makes recommendations on GST rates, exemptions, model GST laws, principles of levy, apportionment of inter-State supplies, special provisions for certain States and other GST-related matters.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a matter on which the GST Council makes recommendations?

options.A: Model GST laws
options.B: Audit of government expenditure

questions.explanation: The GST Council makes recommendations on GST rates, exemptions, model GST laws, principles of levy, apportionment of inter-State supplies, special provisions for certain States and other GST-related matters.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a matter on which the GST Council makes recommendations?

options.A: Principles of levy
options.B: Audit of government receipts

questions.explanation: The GST Council makes recommendations on GST rates, exemptions, model GST laws, principles of levy, apportionment of inter-State supplies, special provisions for certain States and other GST-related matters.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a matter on which the GST Council makes recommendations?

options.A: Apportionment of inter-State supplies
options.B: Audit of government expenditure
options.C: Conduct of elections to State Legislatures

questions.explanation: The GST Council makes recommendations on GST rates, exemptions, model GST laws, principles of levy, apportionment of inter-State supplies, special provisions for certain States and other GST-related matters.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a matter on which the GST Council makes recommendations?

options.A: Special provisions for certain States
options.B: Audit of government receipts

questions.explanation: The GST Council makes recommendations on GST rates, exemptions, model GST laws, principles of levy, apportionment of inter-State supplies, special provisions for certain States and other GST-related matters.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a member of the GST Council?

options.A: The Union Finance Minister as Chairperson
options.B: The Chief Justice of India

questions.explanation: The GST Council includes the Union Finance Minister as Chairperson, the Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue or Finance, and the State Finance/Taxation Ministers or other nominated ministers of each State.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a member of the GST Council?

options.A: The Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue or Finance
options.B: The Chief Justice of India

questions.explanation: The GST Council includes the Union Finance Minister as Chairperson, the Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue or Finance, and the State Finance/Taxation Ministers or other nominated ministers of each State.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a member of the GST Council?

options.A: The State Finance/Taxation Ministers or other nominated ministers of each State
options.B: The Chief Justice of India

questions.explanation: The GST Council includes the Union Finance Minister as Chairperson, the Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue or Finance, and the State Finance/Taxation Ministers or other nominated ministers of each State.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a function of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes?

options.A: Investigating and monitoring constitutional and legal safeguards for Scheduled Castes
options.B: Auditing government expenditure

questions.explanation: The NCSC investigates and monitors constitutional and legal safeguards for Scheduled Castes, inquires into complaints, advises on socio-economic development and reports to the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a function of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes?

options.A: Inquiring into complaints
options.B: Auditing government receipts

questions.explanation: The NCSC investigates and monitors safeguards, inquires into complaints, advises on socio-economic development and reports to the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a function of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes?

options.A: Advising on socio-economic development
options.B: Auditing government expenditure

questions.explanation: The NCSC advises on socio-economic development of Scheduled Castes, among its functions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a function of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?

options.A: Monitoring safeguards for Scheduled Tribes
options.B: Auditing government expenditure

questions.explanation: The NCST monitors safeguards for Scheduled Tribes, investigates complaints, advises on development and submits reports to the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a function of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?

options.A: Investigating complaints
options.B: Auditing government receipts

questions.explanation: The NCST investigates complaints relating to safeguards for Scheduled Tribes.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a function of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?

options.A: Advising on development
options.B: Auditing government expenditure

questions.explanation: The NCST advises on development of Scheduled Tribes, among its functions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The National Commission for Backward Classes performs functions assigned by:

options.A: The Constitution and law
options.B: The President only

questions.explanation: The NCBC is a constitutional body concerned with safeguards for socially and educationally backward classes and performs functions assigned by the Constitution and law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: What is the function of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities under Article 350B?

options.A: To investigate matters relating to safeguards for linguistic minorities and report to the President
options.B: To audit government expenditure

questions.explanation: Under Article 350B, the President appoints a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities to investigate matters relating to safeguards for linguistic minorities and report to the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following functions may the Inter-State Council perform?

options.A: Inquiring into and advising upon disputes between States
options.B: Auditing government expenditure

questions.explanation: The Inter-State Council may inquire into and advise upon disputes between States, investigate and discuss subjects of common interest, and recommend better coordination of policy and action.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following functions may the Inter-State Council perform?

options.A: Investigating and discussing subjects of common interest
options.B: Auditing government receipts

questions.explanation: The Inter-State Council may investigate and discuss subjects of common interest among its functions under Article 263.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following functions may the Inter-State Council perform?

options.A: Recommending better coordination of policy and action
options.B: Auditing government expenditure

questions.explanation: The Inter-State Council may recommend better coordination of policy and action among its functions under Article 263.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Election Commission's composition is correct?

options.A: The Commission currently functions with one CEC and two Election Commissioners, though the Constitution permits the President to determine the number
options.B: The Commission currently functions with one CEC and four Election Commissioners
options.C: The Commission has no Election Commissioners
options.D: The Commission consists of three CECs

questions.explanation: The Commission currently functions with one CEC and two Election Commissioners, though the Constitution permits the President to determine the number.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Election Commission's term under the 2023 Act is correct?

options.A: The term is six years or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier, and there is no reappointment
options.B: The term is five years or until attaining 62 years of age, with reappointment permitted
options.C: The term is during the pleasure of the President

questions.explanation: Under the 2023 Act, the term is six years from the date of assuming office or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier. They are not eligible for reappointment.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Election Commission's appointment committee under the 2023 Act is correct?

options.A: The committee consists of the Prime Minister as Chairperson, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha (or leader of the largest opposition party where no recognised LoP exists), and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister
options.B: The committee consists of the President, the Vice-President and the Prime Minister
options.C: The committee consists of the Chief Justice of India and two senior judges
options.D: The committee consists of the Speaker and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha

questions.explanation: The committee consists of the Prime Minister as Chairperson, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha (or leader of the largest opposition party where no recognised LoP exists), and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister. A Search Committee headed by the Cabinet Secretary prepares a panel for consideration.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Who heads the Search Committee that prepares a panel for Election Commission appointments under the 2023 Act?

options.A: The Cabinet Secretary
options.B: The Chief Justice of India

questions.explanation: A Search Committee headed by the Cabinet Secretary prepares a panel for consideration.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the removal of the CEC is correct?

options.A: The CEC can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court Judge, on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity, following a parliamentary address supported by the prescribed special majority in each House and an order of the President
options.B: The CEC can be removed by the President at pleasure
options.C: The CEC can be removed by a simple majority of the Lok Sabha
options.D: The CEC can be removed by the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: The CEC can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court: on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity, following a parliamentary address supported by the prescribed special majority in each House and an order of the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the removal of an Election Commissioner other than the CEC is correct?

options.A: An Election Commissioner or Regional Commissioner cannot be removed from office except on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner
options.B: An Election Commissioner can be removed by the President at pleasure
options.C: An Election Commissioner can be removed by the Prime Minister
options.D: An Election Commissioner can be removed by Parliament by simple majority

questions.explanation: Under the proviso to Article 324(5), an Election Commissioner or Regional Commissioner cannot be removed from office except on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner. This protection is distinct from the removal procedure applicable to the CEC.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for one general electoral roll for every territorial constituency?

options.A: Article 325
options.B: Article 326

questions.explanation: Article 325 provides for one general electoral roll for every territorial constituency and prohibits exclusion from, or a claim to inclusion in, a special electoral roll on grounds only of religion, race, caste or sex.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Article 325 prohibits exclusion from a special electoral roll on grounds only of:

options.A: Religion, race, caste or sex
options.B: Language and region

questions.explanation: Article 325 prohibits exclusion from, or a claim to inclusion in, a special electoral roll on grounds only of religion, race, caste or sex.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Article 326 provides for elections on the basis of:

options.A: Adult suffrage
options.B: Property qualifications

questions.explanation: Article 326 provides for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies on the basis of adult suffrage, subject to constitutional and statutory qualifications.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Article 328 gives power to make laws on State Legislature elections to:

options.A: State Legislatures, subject to parliamentary law
options.B: Parliament only

questions.explanation: Article 328 gives State Legislatures power to make laws on State Legislature elections, subject to parliamentary law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 329, court interference in electoral matters is generally barred except:

options.A: Through election petitions in the manner provided by law
options.B: Through writ petitions in the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: Article 329 generally bars court interference in electoral matters except through election petitions in the manner provided by law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Article 315 provides for:

options.A: A Public Service Commission for the Union and a Public Service Commission for each State
options.B: Only the UPSC

questions.explanation: Article 315 provides for a Public Service Commission for the Union and a Public Service Commission for each State. Two or more States may agree to have a Joint State Public Service Commission.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 316, a UPSC member holds office for:

options.A: Six years from the date of entering office or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
options.B: Six years or until attaining 62 years of age, whichever is earlier
options.C: Five years or until attaining 60 years of age, whichever is earlier
options.D: During the pleasure of the President

questions.explanation: Under Article 316, UPSC members hold office for six years from the date they enter office or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 317, the President may remove a UPSC member on grounds of misbehaviour after:

options.A: The Supreme Court, on a reference by the President, conducts an inquiry and reports that the member ought to be removed
options.B: A parliamentary resolution is passed

questions.explanation: Under Article 317, the President may remove a member on grounds of misbehaviour after the Supreme Court, on a reference by the President, conducts an inquiry and reports that the member ought to be removed.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 317, the President may also remove a UPSC member in specified cases such as:

options.A: Insolvency, paid employment outside official duties, or infirmity of mind or body
options.B: Only misbehaviour
options.D: Only on a Supreme Court recommendation

questions.explanation: The President may also remove a member in specified cases such as insolvency, paid employment outside official duties, or infirmity of mind or body.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 320, the UPSC may assist two or more States when:

options.A: Requested and approved as constitutionally required
options.B: The President orders it without any request

questions.explanation: The UPSC may also assist two or more States when requested and approved as constitutionally required, among its functions under Article 320.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Article 322 provides that the expenses of the UPSC, including salaries, allowances and pensions of its members and staff, are:

options.A: Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: Voted annually by Parliament
options.C: Charged on the Contingency Fund of India
options.D: Met from the Public Account of India

questions.explanation: Under Article 322, the expenses of the UPSC, including salaries, allowances and pensions of its members and staff, are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 316, the Chairman and members of a State Public Service Commission are appointed by:

options.A: The Governor of the State
options.B: The President of India
options.D: The Chief Justice of the High Court

questions.explanation: The Governor of the State appoints the Chairman and members of the State Public Service Commission under Article 316.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 317, the power to remove the Chairman or a member of a State Public Service Commission lies with:

options.A: The President of India
options.B: The Governor of the State
options.D: The Chief Justice of the High Court

questions.explanation: The President of India — not the Governor — has the power of removal under Article 317. For removal on the ground of misbehaviour, the Supreme Court inquiry procedure applies.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 323, a State PSC submits its annual report to the Governor, who causes it and a memorandum explaining non-acceptance of advice to be laid before:

options.A: The State Legislature
options.B: Parliament

questions.explanation: A State PSC submits its annual report to the Governor under Article 323. The Governor causes the report and a memorandum explaining cases where the advice was not accepted to be laid before the State Legislature.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 315(2), a Joint State Public Service Commission may be provided for by:

options.A: Parliament by law; its members are appointed by the President
options.B: The Governor by executive order; its members are appointed by the Governor
options.D: The President by ordinance; its members are appointed by the Governors

questions.explanation: Under Article 315(2), two or more States may agree to have one Public Service Commission serving their needs. Parliament may provide for its establishment by law. Its members are appointed by the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission in which Part of the Constitution?

options.A: Part XII
options.B: Part V

questions.explanation: Article 280, in Part XII of the Constitution, provides for the Finance Commission.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 280, the President constitutes the Finance Commission:

options.A: Every fifth year or at such earlier time as the President considers necessary
options.B: Every year

questions.explanation: The President constitutes the Finance Commission by order every fifth year or at such earlier time as the President considers necessary. It consists of a Chairman and four other members.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 275, grants-in-aid are given from:

options.A: The Consolidated Fund of India to States in need of assistance, as provided by Parliament
options.B: The Contingency Fund of India

questions.explanation: Grants-in-aid under Article 275 are grants from the Consolidated Fund of India to States in need of assistance, as provided by Parliament. The Finance Commission recommends principles governing such grants.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Finance Commission submitted its report to the President on 17 November 2025?

options.A: The Sixteenth Finance Commission
options.B: The Fifteenth Finance Commission

questions.explanation: The Sixteenth Finance Commission was constituted on 31 December 2023, chaired by Dr. Arvind Panagariya, and submitted its report to the President on 17 November 2025.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 243I, the State Finance Commission is constituted by:

options.A: The Governor every fifth year
options.B: The President every fifth year
options.D: The State Legislature every third year

questions.explanation: Under Article 243I, the Governor constitutes a State Finance Commission every fifth year to review the financial position of Panchayats and recommend principles for sharing State revenues, grants and measures to improve their financial position.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Article 243Y extends the State Finance Commission review role to:

options.A: Municipalities
options.B: Panchayats only

questions.explanation: Article 243Y deals with the corresponding State Finance Commission review in relation to Municipalities.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 148, the CAG is appointed by the President by:

options.A: Warrant under his or her hand and seal
options.B: A simple executive order

questions.explanation: The President appoints the CAG by warrant under his or her hand and seal under Article 148.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Article 148(4) provides that after ceasing to hold office, the CAG is:

options.A: Not eligible for further office under the Government of India or under the Government of any State
options.B: Eligible for any government office
options.C: Eligible for office after a two-year cooling-off period
options.D: Eligible only for a judicial office

questions.explanation: Article 148(4) provides that the CAG is not eligible for further office, either under the Government of India or under the Government of any State, after ceasing to hold office.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 151, State audit reports are submitted to the Governor, who causes them to be laid before:

options.A: The State Legislature
options.B: Parliament

questions.explanation: State audit reports are submitted to the Governor, who causes them to be laid before the State Legislature under Article 151.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 150, the accounts of the Union and States are kept in such form as:

options.A: The President may, on the advice of the CAG, prescribe
options.B: Parliament may by law prescribe

questions.explanation: Article 150 provides that the accounts of the Union and States are to be kept in such form as the President may, on the advice of the CAG, prescribe.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The CAG's Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service Act was enacted in which year?
questions.explanation: The Comptroller and Auditor-General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 gives statutory detail to the CAG's mandate.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The Attorney General of India is the:

options.A: Highest law officer of the Union Government
options.B: Highest law officer of a State Government

questions.explanation: Article 76 of the Constitution provides for the Attorney General for India, the highest law officer of the Union Government.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 76, the Attorney General is appointed by the President and must be a person qualified to be appointed:

options.A: A Judge of the Supreme Court
options.B: A Judge of a High Court
options.C: A member of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: The person must be qualified to be appointed a Judge of the Supreme Court. Broadly, this requires Indian citizenship and satisfaction of one of the constitutional experience or distinction criteria prescribed for Supreme Court judges.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 76(3), the Attorney General has the right of audience in:

options.A: All courts in the territory of India
options.B: Only the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: Article 76(3) gives the Attorney General the right of audience in all courts in the territory of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 76(4), the Attorney General holds office:

options.A: During the pleasure of the President
options.B: For a fixed term of five years
options.C: For six years or until attaining 65 years of age
options.D: During the pleasure of the Chief Justice of India

questions.explanation: The Constitution does not prescribe a fixed tenure. Under Article 76(4), the Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 165, the Advocate General of a State is appointed by the Governor and must be qualified to be appointed:

options.A: A Judge of a High Court
options.B: A Judge of the Supreme Court
options.C: A member of the State Legislature

questions.explanation: The Governor appoints a person qualified to be appointed a Judge of a High Court as Advocate General under Article 165.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Article 243K provides for elections to:

options.A: Panchayats
options.B: Municipalities

questions.explanation: Article 243K provides for elections to Panchayats, and Article 243ZA applies the State Election Commission framework to Municipalities.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Article 243ZA applies the State Election Commission framework to:

options.A: Municipalities
options.B: Panchayats

questions.explanation: Article 243ZA applies the State Election Commission framework to Municipalities.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 279A, the GST Council is constituted by:

options.A: The President
options.B: Parliament

questions.explanation: Article 279A provides for the GST Council. The President constitutes it; it includes the Union Finance Minister as Chairperson, the Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue or Finance, and the State Finance/Taxation Ministers or other nominated ministers of each State.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 338, the National Commission for Scheduled Castes reports to:

options.A: The President
options.B: The Prime Minister

questions.explanation: The NCSC investigates and monitors constitutional and legal safeguards for Scheduled Castes, inquires into complaints, advises on socio-economic development and reports to the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 338A, the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes submits reports to:

options.A: The President
options.B: The Governor

questions.explanation: The NCST monitors safeguards for Scheduled Tribes, investigates complaints, advises on development and submits reports to the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 350B, the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is appointed by:

options.A: The President
options.B: The Governor

questions.explanation: Under Article 350B, the President appoints a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities to investigate matters relating to safeguards for linguistic minorities and report to the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Under Article 263, the Inter-State Council may be established by:

options.A: The President, if it appears that public interests would be served by its establishment
options.B: Parliament by law

questions.explanation: Article 263 empowers the President to establish an Inter-State Council if it appears that public interests would be served by its establishment.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Article 243ZD provides for District Planning Committees to:

options.A: Consolidate plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities in a district
options.B: Prepare draft development plans for metropolitan areas

questions.explanation: Article 243ZD provides for District Planning Committees to consolidate plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities in a district.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Article 243ZE provides for Metropolitan Planning Committees to:

options.A: Prepare draft development plans for metropolitan areas
options.B: Consolidate plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities in a district

questions.explanation: Article 243ZE provides for Metropolitan Planning Committees to prepare draft development plans for metropolitan areas.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a statutory body?

options.A: National Human Rights Commission
options.B: Election Commission of India

questions.explanation: The National Human Rights Commission is statutory under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. The ECI, UPSC and CAG are constitutional bodies.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is an executive body?

options.A: NITI Aayog
options.B: Election Commission of India

questions.explanation: NITI Aayog is an executive body created by a Union Government resolution.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a constitutional body?

options.A: National Commission for Scheduled Castes
options.B: National Human Rights Commission

questions.explanation: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes is a constitutional body under Article 338. NHRC and CVC are statutory; NITI Aayog is an executive body.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: The Election Commission of India derives its authority from:

options.A: Article 324 of the Constitution
options.B: The Representation of the People Act, 1951
options.C: An executive order of the President

questions.explanation: The Election Commission of India is constitutional under Article 324.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following elections is conducted by the Election Commission of India?

options.A: Election to the office of the President of India
options.B: Election to a Gram Panchayat

questions.explanation: The ECI conducts elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President. Panchayat and Municipal elections are conducted by State Election Commissions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following elections is conducted by the Election Commission of India?

options.A: Election to the office of the Vice-President of India
options.B: Election to a Gram Panchayat

questions.explanation: The ECI conducts elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following elections is conducted by the Election Commission of India?

options.A: Election to a State Legislative Assembly
options.B: Election to a Gram Panchayat

questions.explanation: The ECI conducts elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following elections is conducted by the Election Commission of India?

options.A: Election to the Lok Sabha
options.B: Election to a Gram Panchayat

questions.explanation: The ECI conducts elections to Parliament, including the Lok Sabha, State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following elections is conducted by the Election Commission of India?

options.A: Election to the Rajya Sabha
options.B: Election to a Gram Panchayat

questions.explanation: The ECI conducts elections to Parliament, including the Rajya Sabha, State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Election Commission of India?

options.A: Preparing and supervising electoral rolls
options.B: Issuing the election schedule
options.D: Recognising political parties and allotting election symbols

questions.explanation: Conducting elections to Municipalities is the function of State Election Commissions, not the ECI.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Election Commission of India?

options.A: Monitoring election expenditure
options.B: Enforcing the Model Code of Conduct

questions.explanation: Conducting elections to Panchayats is the function of State Election Commissions, not the ECI.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Election Commission of India?

options.A: Preparing and supervising electoral rolls
options.B: Issuing the election schedule

questions.explanation: Auditing government expenditure is the function of the CAG, not the ECI.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Election Commission of India?

options.A: Recognising political parties and allotting election symbols
options.B: Monitoring election expenditure
options.C: Recommending distribution of taxes between the Union and States
options.D: Enforcing the Model Code of Conduct

questions.explanation: Recommending distribution of taxes is the function of the Finance Commission, not the ECI.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Election Commission of India?

options.A: Supervising polling and counting
options.B: Advising on disqualification matters where the Constitution or law assigns it that role

questions.explanation: Appointing Supreme Court judges is not a function of the ECI. The ECI supervises polling and counting, advises on disqualification matters where assigned, and prepares and supervises electoral rolls.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the UPSC under Article 320?

options.A: Conducting examinations for appointments to Union services
options.B: Advising on appointments, promotions and transfers
options.D: Advising on disciplinary matters affecting civil servants

questions.explanation: Conducting elections to Parliament is the function of the ECI, not the UPSC.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the UPSC under Article 320?

options.A: Assisting in recruitment methods
options.B: Performing other functions assigned by the Constitution or law
options.D: Advising on disciplinary matters affecting civil servants

questions.explanation: Auditing government expenditure is the function of the CAG, not the UPSC.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Finance Commission?

options.A: Recommending distribution between the Union and States of the net proceeds of shareable taxes
options.B: Recommending allocation of the States' shares among the States
options.D: Recommending principles governing grants-in-aid to States

questions.explanation: Auditing government receipts and expenditure is the function of the CAG, not the Finance Commission.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Finance Commission?

options.A: Recommending measures to augment State Consolidated Funds to supplement Panchayat and Municipal resources
options.B: Recommending principles governing grants-in-aid to States
options.D: Recommending distribution of the net proceeds of shareable taxes between the Union and States

questions.explanation: Conducting elections to Parliament is the function of the ECI, not the Finance Commission.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about the CAG?

options.A: The CAG is appointed by the President by warrant under his or her hand and seal
options.B: The CAG can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court Judge
options.C: The CAG is a member of Parliament
options.D: The CAG audits receipts as well as expenditure

questions.explanation: The CAG is an independent constitutional authority and is neither a member of Parliament nor a judicial officer.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about the CAG?

options.A: The CAG is the guardian of the public purse
options.B: The CAG is part of the judiciary
options.C: The CAG audits government receipts and expenditure
options.D: The CAG is not eligible for further office after retirement

questions.explanation: The CAG is an independent constitutional authority and is not a judicial officer.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about the CAG?

options.A: The CAG audits only expenditure, not receipts
options.B: The CAG audits government receipts and expenditure
options.C: The CAG's reports are examined by the Public Accounts Committee
options.D: The CAG is appointed by the President

questions.explanation: The CAG audits receipts as well as expenditure, including revenue collection, transactions from public funds, government accounts, stores and stock, and entities covered by the Constitution and the 1971 Act.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about the Attorney General of India?

options.A: The Attorney General is appointed by the President
options.B: The Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President
options.C: The Attorney General has a fixed tenure of six years
options.D: The Attorney General has the right of audience in all courts in the territory of India

questions.explanation: The Constitution does not prescribe a fixed tenure. Under Article 76(4), the Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about the Attorney General of India?

options.A: The Attorney General is a member of the Union Cabinet
options.B: The Attorney General is the chief legal adviser to the Union Government
options.C: The Attorney General can speak and take part in parliamentary proceedings under Article 88
options.D: The Attorney General must be qualified to be a Supreme Court judge

questions.explanation: The Attorney General is the chief legal adviser to the Union Government but is not a member of the Council of Ministers merely by holding that office.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about the Attorney General of India?

options.A: The Attorney General has the right to vote in Parliament under Article 88
options.B: The Attorney General has the right to speak and take part in parliamentary proceedings under Article 88
options.C: The Attorney General advises the Government of India on legal matters referred by the President
options.D: The Attorney General has the right of audience in all courts in the territory of India

questions.explanation: Under Article 88, the Attorney General has the right to speak and take part in proceedings but does not have the right to vote by virtue of that Article.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about the Advocate General of a State?

options.A: The Advocate General is appointed by the Governor
options.B: The Advocate General must be qualified to be appointed a Judge of a High Court
options.C: The Advocate General holds office for a fixed term of six years
options.D: The Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor

questions.explanation: The Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor, not for a fixed term.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about the Advocate General of a State?

options.A: The Advocate General is appointed by the President
options.B: The Advocate General advises the State Government on legal matters
options.C: The Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor
options.D: The Advocate General must be qualified to be appointed a Judge of a High Court

questions.explanation: The Advocate General is appointed by the Governor, not the President, under Article 165.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about the State Election Commission?

options.A: The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the President
options.B: The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor
options.C: The State Election Commissioner has constitutionally protected removal conditions comparable to those of a High Court judge
options.D: The State Election Commission conducts elections to Panchayats and Municipalities

questions.explanation: The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor, not the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about the GST Council?

options.A: The GST Council is constituted under Article 279A
options.B: The GST Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister
options.C: The GST Council's recommendations are equivalent to legislation
options.D: The GST Council includes State Finance/Taxation Ministers

questions.explanation: The GST Council's recommendations are constitutionally significant but are not equivalent to legislation.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about the GST Council?

options.A: The GST Council is constituted by the President
options.B: The GST Council is constituted by Parliament
options.C: The GST Council makes recommendations on GST rates and exemptions
options.D: The GST Council includes the Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue or Finance

questions.explanation: The President constitutes the GST Council under Article 279A, not Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about the National Commission for Scheduled Castes?

options.A: The NCSC is provided for under Article 338
options.B: The NCSC investigates and monitors safeguards for Scheduled Castes
options.C: The NCSC reports to the Prime Minister

questions.explanation: The NCSC reports to the President, not the Prime Minister.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?

options.A: The NCST is provided for under Article 338A
options.B: The NCST monitors safeguards for Scheduled Tribes
options.C: The NCST submits reports to the Governor

questions.explanation: The NCST submits reports to the President, not the Governor.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about the National Commission for Backward Classes?

options.A: The NCBC is provided for under Article 338B
options.B: The NCBC is concerned with safeguards for socially and educationally backward classes
options.C: The NCBC performs functions assigned by the Constitution and law
options.D: The NCBC is a statutory body under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993

questions.explanation: The NCBC is a constitutional body under Article 338B, not a statutory body. The NHRC is statutory under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities?

options.A: The Special Officer is provided for under Article 350B
options.B: The Special Officer is appointed by the President
options.C: The Special Officer reports to the Governor
options.D: The Special Officer investigates matters relating to safeguards for linguistic minorities

questions.explanation: The Special Officer reports to the President, not the Governor.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about the Inter-State Council?

options.A: The Inter-State Council is provided for under Article 263
options.B: The Inter-State Council is established by the President
options.C: The Inter-State Council is established by Parliament by law
options.D: The Inter-State Council may inquire into and advise upon disputes between States

questions.explanation: Article 263 empowers the President to establish an Inter-State Council, not Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about District Planning Committees?

options.A: District Planning Committees are provided for under Article 243ZD
options.B: District Planning Committees consolidate plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities in a district
options.C: District Planning Committees prepare draft development plans for metropolitan areas
options.D: District Planning Committees are constitutional bodies

questions.explanation: Preparing draft development plans for metropolitan areas is the function of Metropolitan Planning Committees under Article 243ZE. District Planning Committees consolidate plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities in a district.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about Metropolitan Planning Committees?

options.A: Metropolitan Planning Committees are provided for under Article 243ZE
options.B: Metropolitan Planning Committees prepare draft development plans for metropolitan areas
options.C: Metropolitan Planning Committees consolidate plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities in a district
options.D: Metropolitan Planning Committees are constitutional bodies

questions.explanation: Consolidating plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities in a district is the function of District Planning Committees under Article 243ZD. Metropolitan Planning Committees prepare draft development plans for metropolitan areas.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution

options.A: Article 338
options.B: Article 338A

questions.explanation: Article 338 provides for the NCSC.

questions.question: Which Article provides for the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?

options.A: Article 338
options.B: Article 338A

questions.explanation: Article 338A provides for the NCST.

options.A: Article 338
options.B: Article 338A

questions.explanation: Article 338B provides for the NCBC.

questions.question: Which Article provides for the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities?

options.A: Article 338
options.B: Article 338A

questions.explanation: Article 350B provides for the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for the Inter-State Council?

options.A: Article 263
options.B: Article 279A

questions.explanation: Article 263 provides for the Inter-State Council.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for District Planning Committees?

options.A: Article 243ZD
options.B: Article 243ZE

questions.explanation: Article 243ZD provides for District Planning Committees.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for Metropolitan Planning Committees?

options.A: Article 243ZD
options.B: Article 243ZE

questions.explanation: Article 243ZE provides for Metropolitan Planning Committees.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following is a central law for the conduct of elections in India?

options.A: The Representation of the People Act, 1950
options.B: The Representation of the People Act, 1951
options.C: The Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952

questions.explanation: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 deals with allocation of seats and electoral rolls; the Representation of the People Act, 1951 deals with conduct of elections, qualifications and disqualifications, corrupt practices and election disputes; the Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952 governs those elections.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Act deals principally with allocation of seats and electoral rolls?

options.A: The Representation of the People Act, 1950
options.B: The Representation of the People Act, 1951
options.C: The Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952

questions.explanation: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 deals principally with allocation of seats and electoral rolls.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Act deals with conduct of elections, qualifications and disqualifications, corrupt practices and election disputes?

options.A: The Representation of the People Act, 1950
options.B: The Representation of the People Act, 1951
options.C: The Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952

questions.explanation: The Representation of the People Act, 1951 deals with conduct of elections, qualifications and disqualifications, corrupt practices and election disputes.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Act governs the elections of the President and Vice-President of India?

options.A: The Representation of the People Act, 1950
options.B: The Representation of the People Act, 1951
options.C: The Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952

questions.explanation: The Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952 governs those elections.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for a Joint State Public Service Commission?

options.A: Article 315(2)
options.B: Article 316

questions.explanation: Under Article 315(2), two or more States may agree to have one Public Service Commission serving their needs. Parliament may provide for its establishment by law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article restricts further employment after a person ceases to hold office as a member or Chairman of a Public Service Commission?

options.A: Article 319
options.B: Article 320

questions.explanation: Article 319 restricts further employment after a person ceases to hold office as a member or Chairman of a Public Service Commission. The restrictions differ for the UPSC Chairman, UPSC members and State PSC members.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Article 323 requires the Government to place before Parliament:

options.A: The UPSC annual report and a memorandum explaining non-acceptance of its advice
options.B: Only the UPSC annual report
options.C: Only a memorandum explaining non-acceptance of advice

questions.explanation: Under Article 323, the Government is constitutionally required to place the UPSC annual report and a memorandum explaining non-acceptance of its advice before Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article governs the removal of State PSC members?

options.A: Article 317
options.B: Article 316

questions.explanation: Under Article 317, the President has the power of removal of State PSC members. For removal on the ground of misbehaviour, the Supreme Court inquiry procedure applies.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article governs the submission of the annual report by a State PSC?

options.A: Article 323
options.B: Article 316

questions.explanation: Under Article 323, a State PSC submits its annual report to the Governor, who causes it and a memorandum explaining non-acceptance of advice to be laid before the State Legislature.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides for grants-in-aid to States in need of assistance?

options.A: Article 275
options.B: Article 280

questions.explanation: Grants-in-aid under Article 275 are grants from the Consolidated Fund of India to States in need of assistance, as provided by Parliament. The Finance Commission recommends principles governing such grants.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article requires the President to lay the Finance Commission's recommendations and an explanatory memorandum before Parliament?

options.A: Article 281
options.B: Article 280

questions.explanation: Under Article 281, the President causes the recommendations and an explanatory memorandum on action taken to be laid before each House of Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides that the CAG performs duties and exercises powers relating to Union and State accounts as prescribed by Parliament?

options.A: Article 149
options.B: Article 148

questions.explanation: Article 149 provides that the CAG performs duties and exercises powers relating to Union and State accounts and other authorities or bodies as prescribed by Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides that Union audit reports are submitted to the President?

options.A: Article 151
options.B: Article 148

questions.explanation: Under Article 151, Union audit reports of the CAG are submitted to the President, who causes them to be laid before each House of Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article gives the Attorney General the right to speak and take part in parliamentary proceedings?

options.A: Article 88
options.B: Article 76

questions.explanation: Under Article 88, the Attorney General has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of either House of Parliament, any joint sitting, and any parliamentary committee of which he or she may be named a member, but does not have the right to vote by virtue of that Article.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article provides that the Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President?

options.A: Article 76(4)
options.B: Article 76(1)

questions.explanation: Under Article 76(4), the Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which Article gives the Attorney General the right of audience in all courts in the territory of India?

options.A: Article 76(3)
options.B: Article 76(1)

questions.explanation: Article 76(3) gives the Attorney General the right of audience in all courts in the territory of India.

options.D: Comptroller and Auditor General of India

options.A: Finance Commission of India

options.D: Comptroller and Auditor General of India

options.A: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.B: Election Commission of India

questions.question: According to the primary reference sources, which body's official website is legislative.gov.in?

options.A: Legislative Department — Constitution text, Article 76 and related provisions
options.B: Election Commission of India

questions.explanation: Legislative Department — Constitution text, Article 76 and related provisions (legislative.gov.in).

questions.question: According to the primary reference sources, which body's official website is ncsc.nic.in?

options.A: National Commission for Scheduled Castes

questions.question: According to the exam note, for a question involving a newly amended law or current office-holder, what should be verified?

options.A: The latest Gazette notification and official institutional website
options.B: Only the Constitution text
options.D: Only the annual report of the body

questions.explanation: The exam note states: For a question involving a newly amended law, current appointment or current office-holder, verify the latest Gazette notification and official institutional website. Constitutional provisions remain the controlling source.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: According to the exam note, what remains the controlling source?

options.A: Constitutional provisions
options.B: The latest Gazette notification

questions.explanation: The exam note states that constitutional provisions remain the controlling source.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the ECI and State Election Commissions is correct?

options.A: The ECI conducts elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President; State Election Commissions conduct elections to Panchayats and Municipalities within the State
options.B: The ECI conducts elections to Panchayats and Municipalities; State Election Commissions conduct elections to Parliament
options.C: Both the ECI and State Election Commissions conduct elections to Parliament
options.D: State Election Commissions conduct elections to the offices of President and Vice-President

questions.explanation: The Election Commission of India conducts elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President. State Election Commissions conduct elections to Panchayats and Municipalities within the State.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Finance Commission and State Finance Commission is correct?

options.A: The Finance Commission is constituted under Article 280 by the President; State Finance Commissions are constituted under Article 243I by the Governor
options.B: The Finance Commission is constituted under Article 243I by the Governor; State Finance Commissions are constituted under Article 280 by the President
options.C: Both are constituted under Article 280 by the President
options.D: Both are constituted under Article 243I by the Governor

questions.explanation: The Finance Commission is constituted under Article 280 by the President; State Finance Commissions are constituted under Article 243I by the Governor.
questions.source: Constitutional_Bodies.pdf, Page 4, Section E; Page 6, Section H

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the GST Council and Finance Commission is correct?

options.A: The GST Council is constituted under Article 279A and makes recommendations on GST matters; the Finance Commission is constituted under Article 280 and recommends tax devolution and grants
options.B: The GST Council is constituted under Article 280 and recommends tax devolution; the Finance Commission is constituted under Article 279A and recommends GST rates

questions.explanation: The Finance Commission is constituted under Article 280 and recommends tax devolution and grants. The GST Council is a constitutional joint forum under Article 279A that makes recommendations on key GST matters, including rates, exemptions and model laws.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the CAG and the PAC is correct?

options.A: The CAG is a constitutional body; the PAC is a parliamentary committee that examines CAG reports
options.B: The CAG is a parliamentary committee; the PAC is a constitutional body
options.C: Both the CAG and the PAC are constitutional bodies
options.D: Both the CAG and the PAC are parliamentary committees

questions.explanation: The CAG is a constitutional body; the PAC is a parliamentary committee that examines CAG reports. The CAG assists the PAC by providing audit findings and explanations.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Attorney General and Advocate General is correct?

options.A: The Attorney General is appointed by the President under Article 76; the Advocate General is appointed by the Governor under Article 165
options.B: The Attorney General is appointed by the Governor; the Advocate General is appointed by the President
options.C: Both are appointed by the President
options.D: Both are appointed by the Governor

questions.explanation: The Attorney General of India is appointed by the President under Article 76; the Advocate General is appointed by the Governor under Article 165.
questions.source: Constitutional_Bodies.pdf, Page 6, Sections G and H

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the NCSC, NCST and NCBC is correct?

options.A: NCSC is under Article 338, NCST under Article 338A, and NCBC under Article 338B
options.B: NCSC is under Article 338A, NCST under Article 338B, and NCBC under Article 338

questions.explanation: NCSC — Article 338; NCST — Article 338A; NCBC — Article 338B.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the State Election Commission and State Finance Commission is correct?

options.A: The State Election Commission is under Articles 243K and 243ZA; the State Finance Commission is under Articles 243I and 243Y
options.B: The State Election Commission is under Articles 243I and 243Y; the State Finance Commission is under Articles 243K and 243ZA

questions.explanation: State Election Commission — Articles 243K and 243ZA; State Finance Commission — Articles 243I and 243Y.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the District Planning Committee and Metropolitan Planning Committee is correct?

options.A: District Planning Committees are under Article 243ZD; Metropolitan Planning Committees are under Article 243ZE
options.B: District Planning Committees are under Article 243ZE; Metropolitan Planning Committees are under Article 243ZD

questions.explanation: District Planning Committees — Article 243ZD; Metropolitan Planning Committees — Article 243ZE.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Inter-State Council and GST Council is correct?

options.A: The Inter-State Council is under Article 263; the GST Council is under Article 279A
options.B: The Inter-State Council is under Article 279A; the GST Council is under Article 263

questions.explanation: Inter-State Council — Article 263; GST Council — Article 279A.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the removal of the CEC and a State PSC member is correct?

options.A: Both the CEC and a State PSC member can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court Judge
options.B: The CEC is removed by the President at pleasure; a State PSC member is removed like a Supreme Court Judge
options.C: The CEC is removed like a Supreme Court Judge; a State PSC member is removed by the Governor at pleasure

questions.explanation: The CEC can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court. State PSC members are also removed by the President under Article 317, with the Supreme Court inquiry procedure applying for removal on the ground of misbehaviour.
questions.source: Constitutional_Bodies.pdf, Page 2, Section B; Page 3, Section D

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the appointment of the CEC and a State PSC member is correct?

options.A: The CEC is appointed by the President; a State PSC member is appointed by the Governor
options.B: The CEC is appointed by the Governor; a State PSC member is appointed by the President
options.C: Both are appointed by the President
options.D: Both are appointed by the Governor

questions.explanation: The CEC is appointed by the President; a State PSC member is appointed by the Governor under Article 316.
questions.source: Constitutional_Bodies.pdf, Page 1, Section B; Page 3, Section D

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Election Commission's role in disqualification matters is correct?

options.A: The ECI advises on disqualification matters where the Constitution or law assigns it that role
options.B: The ECI decides all disqualification matters finally
options.C: The ECI has no role in disqualification matters
options.D: The ECI's role in disqualification matters is purely advisory in all cases without exception

questions.explanation: The ECI advises on disqualification matters where the Constitution or law assigns it that role.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Model Code of Conduct is correct?

options.A: The ECI enforces the Model Code of Conduct through its directions
options.B: The Model Code of Conduct is a statutory law enacted by Parliament
options.C: The Model Code of Conduct is enforced by the Supreme Court
options.D: The Model Code of Conduct is enforced by the Finance Commission

questions.explanation: The ECI enforces the Model Code of Conduct through its directions, among its principal functions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the ECI's role in recognising political parties is correct?

options.A: The ECI recognises political parties and allots election symbols under the applicable law and orders
options.B: The ECI has no role in recognising political parties
options.C: Political parties are recognised by the Supreme Court
options.D: Political parties are recognised by the Finance Commission

questions.explanation: The ECI recognises political parties and allots election symbols under the applicable law and orders.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the UPSC's advisory role is correct?

options.A: The UPSC is generally an advisory body; its recommendations are not binding, but non-acceptance must be explained to Parliament
options.B: The UPSC's recommendations are binding in all matters
options.C: The UPSC's recommendations are binding only on disciplinary matters
options.D: The UPSC has no advisory role

questions.explanation: UPSC is generally an advisory body. Its recommendations are not binding, but the Government is constitutionally required under Article 323 to place its annual report and a memorandum explaining non-acceptance of its advice before Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the UPSC's composition guideline is correct?

options.A: As nearly as may be, one-half of the members should have held office for at least ten years under the Government of India or a State Government
options.B: At least one-third of the members should have held office for five years
options.C: All members must have held office for at least fifteen years
options.D: There is no composition guideline in the Constitution

questions.explanation: As nearly as may be, one-half of the members should be persons who have held office for at least ten years under the Government of India or a State Government. This is a constitutional qualification guideline under Article 316.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the State PSC's removal procedure is correct?

options.A: The President removes a State PSC member; for removal on the ground of misbehaviour, the Supreme Court inquiry procedure applies
options.B: The Governor removes a State PSC member at pleasure
options.C: The Chief Minister removes a State PSC member
options.D: The State Legislature removes a State PSC member by resolution

questions.explanation: The President of India — not the Governor — has the power of removal under Article 317. For removal on the ground of misbehaviour, the Supreme Court inquiry procedure applies.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about vertical devolution is correct?

options.A: Vertical devolution is the division of the divisible pool of Union taxes between the Union Government and all State Governments collectively
options.B: Vertical devolution is the distribution of the States' share among individual States
options.C: Vertical devolution is the distribution of grants-in-aid among States
options.D: Vertical devolution is the division of GST revenues between the Union and States

questions.explanation: Vertical devolution is the division of the divisible pool of Union taxes between the Union Government and all State Governments collectively.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about horizontal devolution is correct?

options.A: Horizontal devolution is the distribution of the States' share of the divisible pool among individual States according to criteria recommended by the Finance Commission
options.B: Horizontal devolution is the division of the divisible pool between the Union and States collectively
options.C: Horizontal devolution is the distribution of grants-in-aid among States
options.D: Horizontal devolution is the division of GST revenues between the Union and States

questions.explanation: Horizontal devolution is the distribution of the States' share of the divisible pool among individual States according to the criteria recommended by the Finance Commission.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Finance Commission's composition is correct?

options.A: The Finance Commission consists of a Chairman and four other members
options.B: The Finance Commission consists of a Chairman and two other members
options.C: The Finance Commission consists of a Chairman and six other members
options.D: The Finance Commission consists of three members with no Chairman

questions.explanation: The Finance Commission consists of a Chairman and four other members.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the CAG's role as guardian of the public purse is correct?

options.A: The CAG audits government receipts and expenditure and reports whether public money has been applied in accordance with law, rules and proper financial procedures
options.B: The CAG only audits defence expenditure
options.C: The CAG only audits State government accounts
options.D: The CAG has no role in auditing public money

questions.explanation: The CAG is the guardian of the public purse and the supreme audit institution of India. The CAG audits government receipts and expenditure and reports whether public money has been applied in accordance with law, rules and proper financial procedures.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the CAG's audit of stores and stock is correct?

options.A: The CAG audits stores and stock as part of its audit mandate
options.B: The CAG does not audit stores and stock

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Attorney General's professional restrictions is correct?

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Advocate General's functions is correct?

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the GST Council's composition is correct?

options.D: The GST Council includes only the Prime Minister and Chief Ministers

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the NCSC's constitutional status is correct?

options.B: The NCSC is a statutory body under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the NCST's constitutional status is correct?

options.B: The NCST is a statutory body

options.D: The NCST is a judicial body

options.B: The NCBC is a statutory body

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is correct?

options.B: The Special Officer is appointed by the Governor and reports to the Governor

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Inter-State Council's establishment is correct?

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about District Planning Committees is correct?

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Metropolitan Planning Committees is correct?

options.B: Metropolitan Planning Committees consolidate plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities in a district under Article 243ZD
options.C: Metropolitan Planning Committees conduct elections to Municipalities

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the classification of bodies in India is correct?

options.A: India has constitutional, statutory and executive bodies; for example, NCSC is constitutional, NHRC is statutory, and NITI Aayog is an executive body
options.B: All bodies in India are constitutional bodies
options.C: All bodies in India are statutory bodies
options.D: All bodies in India are executive bodies

questions.explanation: India has constitutional, statutory and executive bodies. For example, NCSC (Article 338) is constitutional; NHRC is statutory; NITI Aayog is an executive body created by a Union Government resolution.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 is correct?

options.B: The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 created the Election Commission, a constitutional body

options.D: The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 created the Finance Commission

questions.explanation: The National Human Rights Commission is statutory under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Election Commission's establishment is correct?

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the ECI's conduct of elections is correct?

options.C: The ECI conducts elections only to the Lok Sabha
options.D: The ECI conducts elections only to State Legislatures

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the ECI's multi-member status is correct?

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the 2023 Act's appointment procedure for the Election Commission is correct?

options.D: The 2023 Act provides for appointment by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Election Commission's term under the 2023 Act is correct?

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the State PSC's reporting is correct?

options.A: A State PSC submits its annual report to the Governor, who causes it and a memorandum explaining non-acceptance of advice to be laid before the State Legislature

options.C: A State PSC submits its annual report directly to the State Legislature
options.D: A State PSC submits its annual report to the Chief Minister

questions.explanation: A State PSC submits its annual report to the Governor under Article 323. The Governor causes the report and a memorandum explaining cases where the advice was not accepted to be laid before the State Legislature.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Finance Commission's role in grants-in-aid is correct?

options.A: The Finance Commission recommends principles governing grants-in-aid to States under Article 275
options.B: The Finance Commission directly disburses grants-in-aid to States
options.D: The Finance Commission has no role in grants-in-aid

questions.explanation: Grants-in-aid under Article 275 are grants from the Consolidated Fund of India to States in need of assistance, as provided by Parliament. The Finance Commission recommends principles governing such grants.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the CAG's audit reports is correct?

options.A: Union audit reports are submitted to the President, who causes them to be laid before each House of Parliament; State audit reports are submitted to the Governor, who causes them to be laid before the State Legislature
options.B: All CAG reports are submitted directly to Parliament
options.C: All CAG reports are submitted to the Supreme Court
options.D: All CAG reports are submitted to the Prime Minister

questions.explanation: Under Article 151, Union audit reports of the CAG are submitted to the President, who causes them to be laid before each House of Parliament. State audit reports are submitted to the Governor, who causes them to be laid before the State Legislature.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the CAG's role in legislative financial committees is correct?

options.A: CAG reports are examined by legislative financial committees, especially the Public Accounts Committee, and the CAG assists the PAC by providing audit findings and explanations
options.B: The CAG is a member of the PAC
options.D: The CAG has no relationship with the PAC

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Attorney General's qualifications is correct?

options.A: The person must be qualified to be appointed a Judge of the Supreme Court, which broadly requires Indian citizenship and satisfaction of one of the constitutional experience or distinction criteria prescribed for Supreme Court judges
options.B: The person must be a member of the Lok Sabha
options.C: The person must have served as a Governor
options.D: The person must be a retired High Court judge

questions.explanation: The person must be qualified to be appointed a Judge of the Supreme Court. Broadly, this requires Indian citizenship and satisfaction of one of the constitutional experience or distinction criteria prescribed for Supreme Court judges.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Advocate General's appointment is correct?

questions.explanation: The Governor appoints the Advocate General, who must be qualified to be appointed a Judge of a High Court.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the State Election Commission's constitutional protection is correct?
