questions.explanation: The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor and has constitutionally protected removal conditions comparable to those of a High Court judge.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the retirement ages of UPSC and State PSC members is correct?

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the appointment and removal of UPSC and State PSC members is correct?

options.A: UPSC members are appointed by the President; State PSC members are appointed by the Governor; removal in both cases is by the President
options.B: UPSC members are appointed by the Governor; State PSC members are appointed by the President; removal in both cases is by the Governor

options.D: Both UPSC and State PSC members are appointed and removed by the Governor

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the reporting of UPSC and State PSC is correct?

options.C: Both report to the Governor for placement before the State Legislature
options.D: The UPSC reports to the Governor; a State PSC reports to the President

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the expenses charged on the Consolidated Fund is correct?

options.D: No constitutional body's expenses are charged on the Consolidated Fund

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the frequency of constitution of the Finance Commission and State Finance Commission is correct?

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the distinction between the ECI and State Election Commissions is correct?

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Election Commission and the National Human Rights Commission is correct?

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the CAG's removal is correct?

options.B: The Advocate General holds office for a fixed term of six years
options.C: The Advocate General holds office until attaining 62 years of age
options.D: The Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the President

questions.explanation: The Advocate General advises the State Government on legal matters and holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Governor's role in appointments is correct?

options.A: The Governor appoints the Advocate General, State PSC members, and the State Election Commissioner
options.B: The Governor appoints the Attorney General and the CAG
options.C: The Governor appoints the Finance Commission Chairman
options.D: The Governor appoints the UPSC Chairman

questions.explanation: The Governor appoints the Advocate General (Article 165), State PSC members (Article 316), and the State Election Commissioner (Articles 243K and 243ZA).
questions.source: Constitutional_Bodies.pdf, Page 6, Sections G and H; Page 3, Section D

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the President's role in appointments is correct?

options.A: The President appoints the CEC and Election Commissioners, UPSC members, the CAG, the Attorney General, the Finance Commission, the GST Council, and the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
options.B: The President appoints only the CAG
options.C: The President appoints only the Attorney General
options.D: The President appoints the State Election Commissioner

questions.explanation: The President appoints the CEC and Election Commissioners, UPSC members, the CAG, the Attorney General, the Finance Commission, the GST Council, and the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, among others.
questions.source: Constitutional_Bodies.pdf, Sections B, C, E, F, G and H

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the removal of constitutional body heads is correct?

options.A: The CEC and the CAG can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court Judge; UPSC members can be removed after a Supreme Court inquiry on a reference by the President
options.B: All constitutional body heads can be removed by the President at pleasure
options.C: All constitutional body heads can be removed by Parliament by simple majority
options.D: All constitutional body heads can be removed by the Supreme Court directly

questions.explanation: The CEC and the CAG can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court Judge. UPSC members can be removed on grounds of misbehaviour after a Supreme Court inquiry on a reference by the President, or in specified cases such as insolvency, paid employment outside official duties, or infirmity of mind or body.
questions.source: Constitutional_Bodies.pdf, Page 2, Section B; Page 3, Section C; Page 5, Section F

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the composition of the Election Commission is correct?

options.A: Under Article 324(2), it consists of the CEC and such number of other Election Commissioners as the President may from time to time fix; the Constitution itself does not permanently prescribe a fixed number
options.B: The Constitution permanently fixes the number at three
options.C: The Constitution permanently fixes the number at two
options.D: The Constitution permanently fixes the number at five

questions.explanation: Under Article 324(2), it consists of the Chief Election Commissioner and such number of other Election Commissioners as the President may from time to time fix. The Constitution itself does not permanently prescribe a fixed number.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Election Commission's multi-member status is correct?

options.A: Two additional Election Commissioners were appointed on 1 October 1993; the Commission currently functions with one CEC and two Election Commissioners
options.B: The Commission currently functions with one CEC and four Election Commissioners
options.C: The Commission currently functions with three CECs
options.D: The Commission currently functions with one CEC and no Election Commissioners

questions.explanation: Two additional Election Commissioners were appointed on 1 October 1993; the multi-member arrangement has continued since then. The Commission currently functions with one CEC and two Election Commissioners, though the Constitution permits the President to determine the number.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the National Voters' Day is correct?

options.A: National Voters' Day is observed on 25 January every year, marking the establishment of the Election Commission of India
options.B: National Voters' Day is observed on 26 January every year
options.C: National Voters' Day is observed on 15 August every year
options.D: National Voters' Day is observed on 26 November every year

questions.explanation: National Voters' Day is observed on 25 January every year, marking the establishment of the Election Commission of India on 25 January 1950.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act is correct?

options.A: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years
options.B: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 increased the voting age from 18 to 21 years
options.C: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 created the Election Commission
options.D: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 created the Finance Commission

questions.explanation: The voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the 104th Amendment framework and the Lok Sabha is correct?

options.A: The constitutional maximum is 550 members; the nominated Anglo-Indian seats ceased after the 104th Amendment
options.B: The constitutional maximum is 545 members

questions.explanation: The constitutional maximum is 550 members; the nominated Anglo-Indian seats ceased after the 104th Amendment.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Election Commission and local body elections is correct?

options.A: The ECI does not conduct elections to local self-government institutions; under Articles 243K and 243ZA, elections to Panchayats and Municipalities are vested in State Election Commissions
options.B: The ECI conducts all local body elections
options.C: The ECI conducts only Municipal elections
options.D: The ECI conducts only Panchayat elections

questions.explanation: No. Under Articles 243K and 243ZA, elections to Panchayats and Municipalities are vested in State Election Commissions. The ECI conducts elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Election Commission's role in disqualification matters is correct?

options.A: The ECI advises on disqualification matters where the Constitution or law assigns it that role
options.B: The ECI has no role in disqualification matters
options.C: The ECI decides all disqualification matters finally
options.D: The ECI's role in disqualification matters is purely advisory in all cases without exception

questions.explanation: The ECI advises on disqualification matters where the Constitution or law assigns it that role.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the UPSC's advice and Article 323 is correct?

options.A: The UPSC's recommendations are not binding, but the Government must place the annual report and a memorandum explaining non-acceptance of advice before Parliament under Article 323
options.B: The UPSC's recommendations are binding in all matters
options.C: The UPSC's recommendations are binding only on disciplinary matters
options.D: The Government need not report non-acceptance of UPSC advice

questions.explanation: UPSC is generally an advisory body. Its recommendations are not binding, but the Government is constitutionally required under Article 323 to place its annual report and a memorandum explaining non-acceptance of its advice before Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the State PSC's removal procedure is correct?

options.A: The President removes a State PSC member; for removal on the ground of misbehaviour, the Supreme Court inquiry procedure applies
options.B: The Governor removes a State PSC member at pleasure
options.C: The Chief Minister removes a State PSC member
options.D: The State Legislature removes a State PSC member by resolution

questions.explanation: The President of India — not the Governor — has the power of removal under Article 317. For removal on the ground of misbehaviour, the Supreme Court inquiry procedure applies.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Joint State Public Service Commission is correct?

options.A: Under Article 315(2), two or more States may agree to have one Public Service Commission serving their needs; Parliament may provide for its establishment by law, and its members are appointed by the President
options.B: A Joint State PSC is established by the Governor by executive order
options.C: A Joint State PSC's members are appointed by the Governors of the concerned States
options.D: A Joint State PSC is established by the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: Under Article 315(2), two or more States may agree to have one Public Service Commission serving their needs. Parliament may provide for its establishment by law. Its members are appointed by the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Finance Commission and Article 275 is correct?

options.A: Grants-in-aid under Article 275 are grants from the Consolidated Fund of India to States in need of assistance, as provided by Parliament, with the Finance Commission recommending principles governing such grants
options.B: Grants-in-aid are given from the Contingency Fund of India
options.C: Grants-in-aid are given by the RBI
options.D: Grants-in-aid are given by the GST Council

questions.explanation: Grants-in-aid under Article 275 are grants from the Consolidated Fund of India to States in need of assistance, as provided by Parliament. The Finance Commission recommends principles governing such grants.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the divisible pool of Union taxes is correct?

options.A: Cesses and surcharges levied for Union purposes are generally outside the divisible pool
options.B: Cesses and surcharges are always part of the divisible pool
options.C: The divisible pool includes all Union taxes without exception
options.D: The divisible pool consists only of GST

questions.explanation: The divisible pool is the net proceeds of Union taxes that are shareable with States under the constitutional scheme, excluding taxes and duties that are constitutionally excluded from distribution and subject to applicable provisions. Cesses and surcharges levied for Union purposes are generally outside the divisible pool.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Sixteenth Finance Commission is correct?

options.A: It was constituted on 31 December 2023, chaired by Dr. Arvind Panagariya, and submitted its report to the President on 17 November 2025; its recommendations cover 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031
options.B: It was constituted on 1 April 2026 and submitted its report on 31 March 2031
options.C: It was constituted on 17 November 2025 and submitted its report on 31 December 2023
options.D: It was constituted on 1 January 2024 and submitted its report on 1 January 2026

questions.explanation: The Sixteenth Finance Commission was constituted on 31 December 2023, chaired by Dr. Arvind Panagariya, and submitted its report to the President on 17 November 2025. Its recommendations cover the five-year period beginning 1 April 2026 and ending 31 March 2031.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the CAG's audit mandate under Article 149 is correct?

options.A: The CAG performs duties and exercises powers relating to Union and State accounts and other authorities or bodies as prescribed by Parliament; the 1971 Act gives statutory detail to this mandate
options.B: The CAG audits only Union accounts
options.C: The CAG audits only State accounts
options.D: The CAG audits only defence accounts

questions.explanation: Article 149 provides that the CAG performs duties and exercises powers relating to Union and State accounts and other authorities or bodies as prescribed by Parliament. The CAG's Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service Act, 1971 gives statutory detail to this mandate.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the CAG's role in auditing revenue collection is correct?

options.A: The CAG audits revenue collection as part of its audit of receipts
options.B: The CAG does not audit revenue collection
options.C: The CAG audits revenue collection only for the Union Government
options.D: The CAG audits revenue collection only for State Governments

questions.explanation: The CAG audits receipts as well as expenditure, including revenue collection, transactions from public funds, government accounts, stores and stock, and entities covered by the Constitution and the 1971 Act.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Attorney General's right of audience is correct?

options.A: Article 76(3) gives the Attorney General the right of audience in all courts in the territory of India
options.B: The Attorney General has the right of audience only in the Supreme Court
options.C: The Attorney General has the right of audience only in High Courts
options.D: The Attorney General has no right of audience in any court

questions.explanation: Article 76(3) gives the Attorney General the right of audience in all courts in the territory of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Attorney General's duties is correct?

options.A: The Attorney General advises the Government of India on legal matters referred by the President, performs legal duties assigned by the President, and discharges functions conferred by the Constitution or other laws
options.B: The Attorney General advises the State Government on legal matters
options.C: The Attorney General audits government expenditure
options.D: The Attorney General conducts elections to Parliament

questions.explanation: The Attorney General advises the Government of India on legal matters referred by the President, performs legal duties assigned by the President, and discharges functions conferred by the Constitution or other laws.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Advocate General's counterpart at the Union level is correct?

options.A: The Advocate General's counterpart at the Union level is the Attorney General of India under Article 76
options.B: The Advocate General's counterpart at the Union level is the Solicitor General
options.C: The Advocate General's counterpart at the Union level is the Chief Justice of India
options.D: The Advocate General has no counterpart at the Union level

questions.explanation: The Advocate General of the State, provided for under Article 165, is the counterpart of the Attorney General at the State level. The Attorney General of India is the highest law officer of the Union under Article 76.
questions.source: Constitutional_Bodies.pdf, Page 6, Sections G and H

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the State Election Commissioner's appointment is correct?

options.A: The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor and has constitutionally protected removal conditions comparable to those of a High Court judge
options.B: The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the President
options.C: The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Chief Minister
options.D: The State Election Commissioner is appointed by Parliament

questions.explanation: The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor and has constitutionally protected removal conditions comparable to those of a High Court judge.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the GST Council's recommendations is correct?

options.A: The GST Council's recommendations are constitutionally significant but are not equivalent to legislation
options.B: The GST Council's recommendations are equivalent to legislation
options.C: The GST Council's recommendations are binding on the Supreme Court
options.D: The GST Council's recommendations require ratification by Parliament

questions.explanation: The GST Council makes recommendations to the Union and States on GST matters. Its recommendations are constitutionally significant but are not equivalent to legislation.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the NCSC's reporting is correct?

options.A: The NCSC reports to the President
options.B: The NCSC reports to the Governor
options.C: The NCSC reports to the Prime Minister
options.D: The NCSC reports directly to Parliament

questions.explanation: The NCSC investigates and monitors constitutional and legal safeguards for Scheduled Castes, inquires into complaints, advises on socio-economic development and reports to the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the NCST's reporting is correct?

options.A: The NCST submits reports to the President
options.B: The NCST submits reports to the Governor
options.C: The NCST submits reports to the Prime Minister
options.D: The NCST submits reports directly to Parliament

questions.explanation: The NCST monitors safeguards for Scheduled Tribes, investigates complaints, advises on development and submits reports to the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities' reporting is correct?

options.A: The Special Officer reports to the President
options.B: The Special Officer reports to the Governor
options.C: The Special Officer reports to the Prime Minister
options.D: The Special Officer reports directly to Parliament

questions.explanation: Under Article 350B, the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities investigates matters relating to safeguards for linguistic minorities and reports to the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Inter-State Council's functions is correct?

options.A: The Inter-State Council may inquire into and advise upon disputes between States, investigate and discuss subjects of common interest, and recommend better coordination of policy and action
options.B: The Inter-State Council conducts elections to Parliament
options.C: The Inter-State Council audits government expenditure
options.D: The Inter-State Council recommends GST rates

questions.explanation: The Inter-State Council may inquire into and advise upon disputes between States, investigate and discuss subjects of common interest, and recommend better coordination of policy and action.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the District Planning Committee's function is correct?

options.A: District Planning Committees consolidate plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities in a district
options.B: District Planning Committees prepare draft development plans for metropolitan areas
options.C: District Planning Committees conduct elections to Panchayats
options.D: District Planning Committees audit Panchayat expenditure

questions.explanation: Article 243ZD provides for District Planning Committees to consolidate plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities in a district.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Metropolitan Planning Committee's function is correct?

options.A: Metropolitan Planning Committees prepare draft development plans for metropolitan areas
options.B: Metropolitan Planning Committees consolidate plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities in a district
options.C: Metropolitan Planning Committees conduct elections to Municipalities
options.D: Metropolitan Planning Committees audit Municipal expenditure

questions.explanation: Article 243ZE provides for Metropolitan Planning Committees to prepare draft development plans for metropolitan areas.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the classification of bodies in India is correct?

options.A: India has constitutional, statutory and executive bodies; for example, NCSC is constitutional, NHRC is statutory, and NITI Aayog is an executive body
options.B: All bodies in India are constitutional bodies
options.C: All bodies in India are statutory bodies
options.D: All bodies in India are executive bodies

questions.explanation: India has constitutional, statutory and executive bodies. For example, NCSC (Article 338) is constitutional; NHRC is statutory; NITI Aayog is an executive body created by a Union Government resolution.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: According to the primary reference sources, the Constitution of India is available from which source?

options.A: Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice
options.B: Election Commission of India

questions.explanation: Constitution of India — Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: According to the primary reference sources, the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 was published in which source?

options.A: Gazette of India
options.B: Election Commission of India website

questions.explanation: Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 — Gazette of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: According to the primary reference sources, the CAG's Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service Act, 1971 is available on which website?

options.A: cag.gov.in
options.B: eci.gov.in

questions.explanation: Comptroller and Auditor General of India — Constitutional provisions, FAQs and CAG's Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service Act, 1971 (cag.gov.in).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: According to the primary reference sources, the Sixteenth Finance Commission reports are available on which website?

options.A: fincomindia.nic.in
options.B: eci.gov.in

questions.explanation: Finance Commission of India — Constitutional Provisions and Sixteenth Finance Commission reports (fincomindia.nic.in).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the constitutional protection of the CAG's independence is correct?

options.A: The CAG can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court Judge, and is not eligible for further office after retirement
options.B: The CAG can be removed by the President at pleasure
options.C: The CAG is eligible for further government office after retirement
options.D: The CAG can be removed by Parliament by simple majority

questions.explanation: The CAG can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court. Article 148(4) provides that the CAG is not eligible for further office, either under the Government of India or under the Government of any State, after ceasing to hold office.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the constitutional protection of the CEC's independence is correct?

options.A: The CEC can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court
options.B: The CEC can be removed by the President at pleasure
options.C: The CEC can be removed by the Prime Minister
options.D: The CEC can be removed by Parliament by simple majority

questions.explanation: The CEC can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court: on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity, following a parliamentary address supported by the prescribed special majority in each House and an order of the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the removal of an Election Commissioner other than the CEC is correct?

options.A: An Election Commissioner or Regional Commissioner cannot be removed from office except on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner
options.B: An Election Commissioner can be removed by the President at pleasure
options.C: An Election Commissioner can be removed by the Prime Minister
options.D: An Election Commissioner can be removed by Parliament by simple majority

questions.explanation: Under the proviso to Article 324(5), an Election Commissioner or Regional Commissioner cannot be removed from office except on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner. This protection is distinct from the removal procedure applicable to the CEC.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the composition of the Election Commission under Article 324(2) is correct?

options.A: It consists of the CEC and such number of other Election Commissioners as the President may from time to time fix; the Constitution itself does not permanently prescribe a fixed number
options.B: The Constitution permanently fixes the number at three
options.C: The Constitution permanently fixes the number at two
options.D: The Constitution permanently fixes the number at five

questions.explanation: Under Article 324(2), it consists of the Chief Election Commissioner and such number of other Election Commissioners as the President may from time to time fix. The Constitution itself does not permanently prescribe a fixed number.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the multi-member status of the Election Commission is correct?

options.A: Two additional Election Commissioners were appointed on 1 October 1993; the Commission currently functions with one CEC and two Election Commissioners
options.B: The Commission currently functions with one CEC and four Election Commissioners
options.C: The Commission currently functions with three CECs
options.D: The Commission currently functions with one CEC and no Election Commissioners

questions.explanation: Two additional Election Commissioners were appointed on 1 October 1993; the multi-member arrangement has continued since then. The Commission currently functions with one CEC and two Election Commissioners, though the Constitution permits the President to determine the number.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the 2023 Act's term of office for the CEC and Election Commissioners is correct?

options.A: Six years from the date of assuming office or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier; they are not eligible for reappointment
options.B: Five years or until attaining 62 years of age, with reappointment permitted
options.C: Ten years or until attaining 70 years of age
options.D: During the pleasure of the President

questions.explanation: Under the 2023 Act, the term is six years from the date of assuming office or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier. They are not eligible for reappointment.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the 2023 Act's appointment committee is correct?

options.A: The committee consists of the Prime Minister as Chairperson, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha (or leader of the largest opposition party where no recognised LoP exists), and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister
options.B: The committee consists of the President, the Vice-President and the Prime Minister
options.C: The committee consists of the Chief Justice of India and two senior judges
options.D: The committee consists of the Speaker and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha

questions.explanation: The committee consists of the Prime Minister as Chairperson, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha (or leader of the largest opposition party where no recognised LoP exists), and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister. A Search Committee headed by the Cabinet Secretary prepares a panel for consideration.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Search Committee for Election Commission appointments is correct?

options.A: A Search Committee headed by the Cabinet Secretary prepares a panel for consideration
options.B: A Search Committee headed by the Chief Justice of India prepares a panel
options.C: A Search Committee headed by the Home Minister prepares a panel

questions.explanation: A Search Committee headed by the Cabinet Secretary prepares a panel for consideration.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the removal of the CEC is correct?

options.A: The CEC can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court: on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity, following a parliamentary address supported by the prescribed special majority in each House and an order of the President
options.B: The CEC can be removed by the President at pleasure
options.C: The CEC can be removed by a simple majority of the Lok Sabha
options.D: The CEC can be removed by the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: The CEC can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court: on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity, following a parliamentary address supported by the prescribed special majority in each House and an order of the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Article 325 is correct?

options.A: Article 325 provides for one general electoral roll for every territorial constituency and prohibits exclusion from, or a claim to inclusion in, a special electoral roll on grounds only of religion, race, caste or sex
options.B: Article 325 provides for adult suffrage
options.C: Article 325 empowers Parliament to make laws on elections
options.D: Article 325 bars court interference in electoral matters

questions.explanation: Article 325 provides for one general electoral roll for every territorial constituency and prohibits exclusion from, or a claim to inclusion in, a special electoral roll on grounds only of religion, race, caste or sex.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Article 326 is correct?

options.A: Article 326 provides for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies on the basis of adult suffrage, subject to constitutional and statutory qualifications
options.B: Article 326 provides for one general electoral roll
options.C: Article 326 empowers Parliament to make laws on elections
options.D: Article 326 bars court interference in electoral matters

questions.explanation: Article 326 provides for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies on the basis of adult suffrage, subject to constitutional and statutory qualifications.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the voting age in India is correct?

options.A: The voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988
options.B: The voting age was increased from 18 to 21 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988
options.C: The voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 years by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976
options.D: The voting age has always been 18 years since 1950

questions.explanation: The voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Article 327 is correct?

options.A: Article 327 empowers Parliament to make laws on elections to legislatures
options.B: Article 327 gives State Legislatures power to make laws on State Legislature elections
options.C: Article 327 bars court interference in electoral matters

questions.explanation: Article 327 empowers Parliament to make laws on elections to legislatures.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Article 328 is correct?

options.A: Article 328 gives State Legislatures power to make laws on State Legislature elections, subject to parliamentary law
options.B: Article 328 empowers Parliament to make laws on elections to legislatures
options.C: Article 328 bars court interference in electoral matters

questions.explanation: Article 328 gives State Legislatures power to make laws on State Legislature elections, subject to parliamentary law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Article 329 is correct?

options.A: Article 329 generally bars court interference in electoral matters except through election petitions in the manner provided by law
options.B: Article 329 provides for adult suffrage
options.C: Article 329 empowers Parliament to make laws on elections
options.D: Article 329 provides for one general electoral roll

questions.explanation: Article 329 generally bars court interference in electoral matters except through election petitions in the manner provided by law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Representation of the People Act, 1950 is correct?

options.A: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 deals principally with allocation of seats and electoral rolls
options.B: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 deals with conduct of elections and election disputes
options.C: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 governs Presidential and Vice-Presidential elections
options.D: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 provides for the appointment of the CEC

questions.explanation: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 deals principally with allocation of seats and electoral rolls.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Representation of the People Act, 1951 is correct?

options.A: The Representation of the People Act, 1951 deals with conduct of elections, qualifications and disqualifications, corrupt practices and election disputes
options.B: The Representation of the People Act, 1951 deals principally with allocation of seats and electoral rolls
options.C: The Representation of the People Act, 1951 governs Presidential and Vice-Presidential elections
options.D: The Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides for the appointment of the CEC

questions.explanation: The Representation of the People Act, 1951 deals with conduct of elections, qualifications and disqualifications, corrupt practices and election disputes.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952 is correct?

options.A: The Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952 governs the elections of the President and Vice-President
options.B: The Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952 governs elections to the Lok Sabha
options.C: The Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952 governs elections to State Legislatures
options.D: The Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952 governs elections to Panchayats

questions.explanation: The Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952 governs those elections.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the UPSC's composition guideline is correct?

options.A: As nearly as may be, one-half of the members should be persons who have held office for at least ten years under the Government of India or a State Government
options.B: At least one-third of the members should have held office for five years
options.C: All members must have held office for at least fifteen years
options.D: There is no composition guideline in the Constitution

questions.explanation: As nearly as may be, one-half of the members should be persons who have held office for at least ten years under the Government of India or a State Government. This is a constitutional qualification guideline under Article 316.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the suspension of a UPSC member is correct?

options.A: The President may suspend the Chairman or another member of the UPSC while a reference concerning removal is pending before the Supreme Court
options.B: The Prime Minister may suspend a member
options.C: The Supreme Court may suspend a member
options.D: A member cannot be suspended during an inquiry

questions.explanation: The President may suspend the Chairman or another member of the UPSC while a reference concerning removal is pending before the Supreme Court.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the removal of UPSC members is correct?

options.A: The President may remove a member on grounds of misbehaviour after the Supreme Court, on a reference by the President, conducts an inquiry and reports that the member ought to be removed
options.B: The President may remove a member at pleasure without any inquiry
options.C: Parliament removes a member by simple majority
options.D: The Chief Justice of India removes a member

questions.explanation: Under Article 317, the President may remove a member on grounds of misbehaviour after the Supreme Court, on a reference by the President, conducts an inquiry and reports that the member ought to be removed.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the specified cases of removal of a UPSC member under Article 317 is correct?

options.A: The President may remove a member in specified cases such as insolvency, paid employment outside official duties, or infirmity of mind or body
options.B: The President may remove a member only on grounds of misbehaviour
options.C: The President may remove a member only on grounds of incapacity
options.D: The President may remove a member only on a Supreme Court recommendation

questions.explanation: The President may also remove a member in specified cases such as insolvency, paid employment outside official duties, or infirmity of mind or body.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the UPSC's assistance to States is correct?

options.A: The UPSC may assist two or more States when requested and approved as constitutionally required
options.B: The UPSC may assist States without any request
options.D: The UPSC assists States only through the Finance Commission

questions.explanation: Under Article 320, the UPSC may also assist two or more States when requested and approved as constitutionally required.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the UPSC's expenses is correct?

options.A: Under Article 322, the expenses of the UPSC, including salaries, allowances and pensions of its members and staff, are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: The UPSC's expenses are voted annually by Parliament
options.C: The UPSC's expenses are charged on the Contingency Fund of India
options.D: The UPSC's expenses are met from the Public Account of India

questions.explanation: Under Article 322, the expenses of the UPSC, including salaries, allowances and pensions of its members and staff, are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the distinction between the UPSC and a departmental recruitment agency is correct?

options.A: The UPSC is a constitutional commission with functions under Articles 315–323, whereas a departmental recruitment board is generally created by executive or statutory arrangements
options.B: The UPSC is a statutory body, whereas a departmental board is constitutional
options.D: The UPSC is an executive body

questions.explanation: UPSC is a constitutional commission with functions under Articles 315–323. A departmental recruitment board or other agency is generally created by executive or statutory arrangements and does not have the same constitutional status.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the State PSC's functions is correct?

options.A: A State PSC conducts examinations for appointments to State services and advises the State Government on recruitment methods, appointments, promotions, transfers and disciplinary matters
options.B: A State PSC audits State government expenditure
options.C: A State PSC conducts elections to the State Legislature
options.D: A State PSC recommends GST rates

questions.explanation: A State PSC conducts examinations for appointments to State services and advises the State Government on recruitment methods, appointments, promotions, transfers and disciplinary matters, subject to constitutional provisions and applicable rules.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the State PSC's annual report is correct?

options.A: A State PSC submits its annual report to the Governor under Article 323, who causes the report and a memorandum explaining non-acceptance of advice to be laid before the State Legislature
options.B: A State PSC submits its annual report to the President, who causes it to be laid before Parliament
options.C: A State PSC submits its annual report directly to the State Legislature
options.D: A State PSC submits its annual report to the Chief Minister

questions.explanation: A State PSC submits its annual report to the Governor under Article 323. The Governor causes the report and a memorandum explaining cases where the advice was not accepted to be laid before the State Legislature.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Finance Commission's recommendations on grants-in-aid is correct?

options.A: The Finance Commission recommends principles governing grants-in-aid to States under Article 275
options.B: The Finance Commission directly disburses grants-in-aid to States
options.D: The Finance Commission has no role in grants-in-aid

questions.explanation: Grants-in-aid under Article 275 are grants from the Consolidated Fund of India to States in need of assistance, as provided by Parliament. The Finance Commission recommends principles governing such grants.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Sixteenth Finance Commission's report submission is correct?

options.A: The Sixteenth Finance Commission submitted its report to the President on 17 November 2025
options.B: The Sixteenth Finance Commission submitted its report to the Prime Minister on 17 November 2025
options.C: The Sixteenth Finance Commission submitted its report to Parliament on 17 November 2025
options.D: The Sixteenth Finance Commission submitted its report to the Supreme Court on 17 November 2025

questions.explanation: The Sixteenth Finance Commission was constituted on 31 December 2023, chaired by Dr. Arvind Panagariya, and submitted its report to the President on 17 November 2025.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the State Finance Commission's review role is correct?

options.A: Under Article 243I, the Governor constitutes a State Finance Commission every fifth year to review the financial position of Panchayats and recommend principles for sharing State revenues, grants and measures to improve their financial position; Article 243Y extends the review role to Municipalities
options.B: Under Article 280, the President constitutes it every fifth year
options.C: Under Article 243K, the Governor constitutes it every year
options.D: Under Article 279A, the GST Council constitutes it

questions.explanation: Under Article 243I, the Governor constitutes a State Finance Commission every fifth year to review the financial position of Panchayats and recommend principles for sharing State revenues, grants and measures to improve their financial position. Article 243Y extends the relevant review role to Municipalities.
questions.source: Constitutional_Bodies.pdf, Page 4, Section E; Page 6, Section H

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the CAG's appointment and removal is correct?

options.A: The President appoints the CAG under Article 148; removal is in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court Judge
options.B: The Prime Minister appoints the CAG; removal by Parliament
options.C: The Chief Justice appoints the CAG; removal by the President
options.D: Parliament appoints the CAG; removal by the President at pleasure

questions.explanation: The President appoints the CAG under Article 148; removal is in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court Judge.
questions.source: Constitutional_Bodies.pdf, Page 5, Section F; Page 7, Section I

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the CAG's audit of receipts and expenditure is correct?

options.A: The CAG audits receipts as well as expenditure, including revenue collection, transactions from public funds, government accounts, stores and stock, and entities covered by the Constitution and the 1971 Act
options.B: The CAG audits only expenditure
options.D: The CAG audits only Union accounts

questions.explanation: The CAG audits receipts as well as expenditure, including revenue collection, transactions from public funds, government accounts, stores and stock, and entities covered by the Constitution and the 1971 Act.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the CAG's relationship with the Public Accounts Committee is correct?

options.A: CAG reports are examined by legislative financial committees, especially the PAC; the CAG assists the PAC by providing audit findings and explanations; the PAC is a parliamentary committee, not a constitutional body
options.B: The CAG is a member of the PAC
options.C: The PAC is a constitutional body

questions.explanation: CAG reports are examined by legislative financial committees, especially the Public Accounts Committee. The CAG assists the PAC by providing audit findings and explanations. The PAC is a parliamentary committee, not a constitutional body.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Attorney General's participation in Parliament is correct?

options.A: Under Article 88, the Attorney General has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of either House, any joint sitting, and any parliamentary committee of which he or she may be named a member, but does not have the right to vote by virtue of that Article
options.B: The Attorney General can vote in Parliament under Article 88
options.C: The Attorney General cannot enter Parliament
options.D: The Attorney General is a member of the Lok Sabha by virtue of office

questions.explanation: Under Article 88, the Attorney General has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of either House of Parliament, any joint sitting, and any parliamentary committee of which he or she may be named a member, but does not have the right to vote by virtue of that Article.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Advocate General's functions is correct?

options.A: The Advocate General advises the State Government on legal matters and holds office during the pleasure of the Governor
options.B: The Advocate General advises the President on legal matters
options.C: The Advocate General holds office for a fixed term of six years
options.D: The Advocate General is a member of the State Cabinet

questions.explanation: The Advocate General advises the State Government on legal matters and holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the State Election Commission's conduct of elections is correct?

options.A: State Election Commissions conduct elections to Panchayats and Municipalities within the State
options.B: State Election Commissions conduct elections to Parliament
options.C: State Election Commissions conduct elections to the offices of President and Vice-President
options.D: State Election Commissions conduct elections to State Legislative Assemblies

questions.explanation: State Election Commissions conduct elections to Panchayats and Municipalities within the State under Articles 243K and 243ZA.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the GST Council's composition and chairperson is correct?

options.A: The GST Council is constituted by the President and chaired by the Union Finance Minister
options.B: The GST Council is constituted by Parliament and chaired by the Prime Minister
options.C: The GST Council is constituted by the President and chaired by the Prime Minister
options.D: The GST Council is constituted by the Union Finance Minister and chaired by the RBI Governor

questions.explanation: The President constitutes the GST Council under Article 279A; it includes the Union Finance Minister as Chairperson, the Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue or Finance, and the State Finance/Taxation Ministers or other nominated ministers of each State.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the GST Council's mandate is correct?

options.A: The GST Council makes recommendations on GST rates, exemptions, model GST laws, principles of levy, apportionment of inter-State supplies, special provisions for certain States and other GST-related matters
options.B: The GST Council audits government expenditure
options.C: The GST Council conducts elections to Parliament
options.D: The GST Council appoints Supreme Court judges

questions.explanation: The GST Council makes recommendations to the Union and States on GST rates, exemptions, model GST laws, principles of levy, apportionment of inter-State supplies, special provisions for certain States and other GST-related matters.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the NCSC's functions is correct?

options.A: The NCSC investigates and monitors constitutional and legal safeguards for Scheduled Castes, inquires into complaints, advises on socio-economic development and reports to the President
options.B: The NCSC audits government expenditure
options.C: The NCSC conducts elections to Parliament

questions.explanation: The NCSC investigates and monitors constitutional and legal safeguards for Scheduled Castes, inquires into complaints, advises on socio-economic development and reports to the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the NCST's functions is correct?

options.A: The NCST monitors safeguards for Scheduled Tribes, investigates complaints, advises on development and submits reports to the President
options.B: The NCST audits government expenditure
options.C: The NCST conducts elections to Parliament

questions.explanation: The NCST monitors safeguards for Scheduled Tribes, investigates complaints, advises on development and submits reports to the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the NCBC's functions is correct?

options.A: The NCBC is a constitutional body concerned with safeguards for socially and educationally backward classes and performs functions assigned by the Constitution and law
options.B: The NCBC audits government expenditure
options.C: The NCBC conducts elections to Parliament

questions.explanation: The NCBC is a constitutional body concerned with safeguards for socially and educationally backward classes and performs functions assigned by the Constitution and law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities' functions is correct?

options.A: The Special Officer investigates matters relating to safeguards for linguistic minorities and reports to the President
options.B: The Special Officer audits government expenditure
options.C: The Special Officer conducts elections to Parliament
options.D: The Special Officer recommends GST rates

questions.explanation: Under Article 350B, the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities investigates matters relating to safeguards for linguistic minorities and reports to the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Inter-State Council's establishment condition is correct?

options.A: The President may establish an Inter-State Council if it appears that public interests would be served by its establishment
options.B: Parliament may establish an Inter-State Council by law
options.C: The Supreme Court may establish an Inter-State Council
options.D: The GST Council may establish an Inter-State Council

questions.explanation: Article 263 empowers the President to establish an Inter-State Council if it appears that public interests would be served by its establishment.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the District Planning Committee's function is correct?

options.A: District Planning Committees consolidate plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities in a district
options.B: District Planning Committees prepare draft development plans for metropolitan areas
options.C: District Planning Committees conduct elections to Panchayats
options.D: District Planning Committees audit Panchayat expenditure

questions.explanation: Article 243ZD provides for District Planning Committees to consolidate plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities in a district.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Metropolitan Planning Committee's function is correct?

options.A: Metropolitan Planning Committees prepare draft development plans for metropolitan areas
options.B: Metropolitan Planning Committees consolidate plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities in a district
options.C: Metropolitan Planning Committees conduct elections to Municipalities
options.D: Metropolitan Planning Committees audit Municipal expenditure

questions.explanation: Article 243ZE provides for Metropolitan Planning Committees to prepare draft development plans for metropolitan areas.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the classification of commissions in India is correct?

options.A: India has constitutional, statutory and executive bodies; for example, NCSC is constitutional, NHRC is statutory, and NITI Aayog is an executive body
options.B: All commissions in India are constitutional bodies
options.C: All commissions in India are statutory bodies
options.D: All commissions in India are executive bodies

questions.explanation: India has constitutional, statutory and executive bodies. For example, NCSC (Article 338) is constitutional; NHRC is statutory; NITI Aayog is an executive body created by a Union Government resolution.

options.B: eci.gov.in

questions.question: According to the primary reference sources, which website provides information on the CAG's constitutional provisions, FAQs and the 1971 Act?

options.A: cag.gov.in
options.B: eci.gov.in

questions.explanation: Comptroller and Auditor General of India — Constitutional provisions, FAQs and CAG's Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service Act, 1971 (cag.gov.in).

questions.question: According to the primary reference sources, which website provides the Constitution text, Article 76 and related provisions?

options.A: legislative.gov.in
options.B: eci.gov.in

questions.explanation: Legislative Department — Constitution text, Article 76 and related provisions (legislative.gov.in).

questions.question: According to the primary reference sources, which website provides information on the constitutional status and functions of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes?

options.A: ncsc.nic.in
options.B: eci.gov.in

questions.explanation: National Commission for Scheduled Castes — Constitutional status and functions (ncsc.nic.in).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: According to the exam note, for a question involving a newly amended law, current appointment or current office-holder, what should be verified?

options.A: The latest Gazette notification and official institutional website
options.B: Only the Constitution text
options.D: Only the annual report of the body

questions.explanation: The exam note states: For a question involving a newly amended law, current appointment or current office-holder, verify the latest Gazette notification and official institutional website. Constitutional provisions remain the controlling source.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: According to the exam note, what remains the controlling source?

options.A: Constitutional provisions
options.B: The latest Gazette notification

questions.explanation: The exam note states that constitutional provisions remain the controlling source.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the ECI and State Election Commissions is correct?

options.A: The ECI conducts elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President; State Election Commissions conduct elections to Panchayats and Municipalities within the State
options.B: The ECI conducts elections to Panchayats and Municipalities; State Election Commissions conduct elections to Parliament
options.C: Both the ECI and State Election Commissions conduct elections to Parliament
options.D: State Election Commissions conduct elections to the offices of President and Vice-President

questions.explanation: The Election Commission of India conducts elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President. State Election Commissions conduct elections to Panchayats and Municipalities within the State.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Finance Commission and State Finance Commission is correct?

options.A: The Finance Commission is constituted under Article 280 by the President; State Finance Commissions are constituted under Article 243I by the Governor
options.B: The Finance Commission is constituted under Article 243I by the Governor; State Finance Commissions are constituted under Article 280 by the President
options.C: Both are constituted under Article 280 by the President
options.D: Both are constituted under Article 243I by the Governor

questions.explanation: The Finance Commission is constituted under Article 280 by the President; State Finance Commissions are constituted under Article 243I by the Governor.
questions.source: Constitutional_Bodies.pdf, Page 4, Section E; Page 6, Section H

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the GST Council and Finance Commission is correct?

options.A: The GST Council is constituted under Article 279A and makes recommendations on GST matters; the Finance Commission is constituted under Article 280 and recommends tax devolution and grants
options.B: The GST Council is constituted under Article 280 and recommends tax devolution; the Finance Commission is constituted under Article 279A and recommends GST rates

questions.explanation: The Finance Commission is constituted under Article 280 and recommends tax devolution and grants. The GST Council is a constitutional joint forum under Article 279A that makes recommendations on key GST matters, including rates, exemptions and model laws.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the CAG and the PAC is correct?

options.A: The CAG is a constitutional body; the PAC is a parliamentary committee that examines CAG reports
options.B: The CAG is a parliamentary committee; the PAC is a constitutional body
options.C: Both the CAG and the PAC are constitutional bodies
options.D: Both the CAG and the PAC are parliamentary committees

questions.explanation: The CAG is a constitutional body; the PAC is a parliamentary committee that examines CAG reports. The CAG assists the PAC by providing audit findings and explanations.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Attorney General and Advocate General is correct?

options.A: The Attorney General is appointed by the President under Article 76; the Advocate General is appointed by the Governor under Article 165
options.B: The Attorney General is appointed by the Governor; the Advocate General is appointed by the President
options.C: Both are appointed by the President
options.D: Both are appointed by the Governor

questions.explanation: The Attorney General of India is appointed by the President under Article 76; the Advocate General is appointed by the Governor under Article 165.
questions.source: Constitutional_Bodies.pdf, Page 6, Sections G and H

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the NCSC, NCST and NCBC is correct?

options.A: NCSC is under Article 338, NCST under Article 338A, and NCBC under Article 338B
options.B: NCSC is under Article 338A, NCST under Article 338B, and NCBC under Article 338

questions.explanation: NCSC — Article 338; NCST — Article 338A; NCBC — Article 338B.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the State Election Commission and State Finance Commission is correct?

options.A: The State Election Commission is under Articles 243K and 243ZA; the State Finance Commission is under Articles 243I and 243Y
options.B: The State Election Commission is under Articles 243I and 243Y; the State Finance Commission is under Articles 243K and 243ZA

questions.explanation: State Election Commission — Articles 243K and 243ZA; State Finance Commission — Articles 243I and 243Y.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the District Planning Committee and Metropolitan Planning Committee is correct?

options.A: District Planning Committees are under Article 243ZD; Metropolitan Planning Committees are under Article 243ZE
options.B: District Planning Committees are under Article 243ZE; Metropolitan Planning Committees are under Article 243ZD

questions.explanation: District Planning Committees — Article 243ZD; Metropolitan Planning Committees — Article 243ZE.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Inter-State Council and GST Council is correct?

options.A: The Inter-State Council is under Article 263; the GST Council is under Article 279A
options.B: The Inter-State Council is under Article 279A; the GST Council is under Article 263

questions.explanation: Inter-State Council — Article 263; GST Council — Article 279A.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the removal of the CEC and a State PSC member is correct?

options.A: Both the CEC and a State PSC member can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court Judge
options.B: The CEC is removed by the President at pleasure; a State PSC member is removed like a Supreme Court Judge
options.C: The CEC is removed like a Supreme Court Judge; a State PSC member is removed by the Governor at pleasure

questions.explanation: The CEC can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court. State PSC members are also removed by the President under Article 317, with the Supreme Court inquiry procedure applying for removal on the ground of misbehaviour.
questions.source: Constitutional_Bodies.pdf, Page 2, Section B; Page 3, Section D

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the appointment of the CEC and a State PSC member is correct?

options.A: The CEC is appointed by the President; a State PSC member is appointed by the Governor
options.B: The CEC is appointed by the Governor; a State PSC member is appointed by the President
options.C: Both are appointed by the President
options.D: Both are appointed by the Governor

questions.explanation: The CEC is appointed by the President; a State PSC member is appointed by the Governor under Article 316.
questions.source: Constitutional_Bodies.pdf, Page 1, Section B; Page 3, Section D

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the CAG's role in auditing government accounts is correct?

options.A: The CAG audits government receipts and expenditure and reports whether public money has been applied in accordance with law, rules and proper financial procedures
options.B: The CAG only audits defence expenditure
options.C: The CAG only audits State government accounts
options.D: The CAG has no role in auditing public money

questions.explanation: The CAG is the guardian of the public purse and the supreme audit institution of India. The CAG audits government receipts and expenditure and reports whether public money has been applied in accordance with law, rules and proper financial procedures.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the CAG's audit of stores and stock is correct?

options.A: The CAG audits stores and stock as part of its audit mandate
options.B: The CAG does not audit stores and stock
options.C: The CAG audits stores and stock only for the Union Government
options.D: The CAG audits stores and stock only for State Governments

questions.explanation: The CAG audits receipts as well as expenditure, including revenue collection, transactions from public funds, government accounts, stores and stock, and entities covered by the Constitution and the 1971 Act.
